As Verstegan has observed, this word is not common to every lord but belongs to the Lord of lords, that is, to God alone and his own. On its etymology, more in Martinius's Etymologicon under the word Deus.

units.la: <bl>Dzugina</bl>, Dolus: unde <bl>Bedzlegen</bl>] Impostor, Sax. ὀρῠ; Impostura ὀρῠεπαφτ: <bl>Dzogh</bl>, & <bl>trogh</bl>, Teutonicis, Fallacia, Impostura: sed & nostratium <bl>tricke</bl>, eodem sensu.
units.tr: Dzugina, deceit, whence Bedzlegen, an impostor. Saxon orth, imposture orthepaftt. Dzogh and trogh, among the Teutonic peoples, mean deceit and imposture. Our own tricke has the same sense.

units.la: <bl>Dzumbon</bl>, Tubis: nunc <bl>trompen</bl>] Huc forte referendum nostrum <bl>Dzum.</bl> Belg. <bl>trommel</bl>. German. <bl>trummen</bl>, i.e. Tympanum: nisi malis è Sax. ὀρῠman, al. ὀρεmian, quod eis jubilare signat, ut & ὀρeam, & ῥῠnὀρeam, jubilum, jubilatio.
units.tr: Dzumbon, trumpets, now trompen. Perhaps our Dzum belongs here, and the Dutch trommel and German trummen, that is, a drum; unless you prefer to derive it from the Saxon ...man or ...mian, which signifies to rejoice, as do ...eam and ...eam, rejoicing and exultation.

units.la: <bl>Dntrt</bl>, Januus] Sax. eâdem notione ὀupa; unde nostratium <bl>dooze</bl>, quod Belgis <bl>Dore</bl>, Teuton. <bl>thur</bl>, ostium.
units.tr: Dntrt, a door-keeper. The Saxon has the same meaning, whence our dooze, which the Dutch call Dore and the Teutonic thur, a door.

units.la: Dumba, Stultus: dumphede, insipientia] Mutus nobis dumbe. Stultus autem non incongrue sic dicendus, propter hebetudinem & vecordiam, muto meritò comparandus; bruto potiùs; unde Stultus, Germanis * Thor, quasi Thier, bruta pecus. Qui autem plus solito tacet, in bis dumps, dicitur.
units.tr: Dumba, foolish; dumphede, folly. Our word dumbe means mute. A fool may not inappropriately be called this, on account of his dullness and madness, and is rightly compared to a mute, or rather to a brute beast. Whence among the Germans Thor means a fool, as if it were Thier, a brute animal. But one who is silent more than usual is said to be in his dumps.

units.la: <bl>Duom</bl>, Judicium: & <bl>duoma</bl>, judicia: & <bl>duomot</bl>, judicatis] His respondet, sono pariter & sensu, Saxon. <bl>dom</bl>, nostratium <bl>doome</bl>, Teuton. <bl>doem</bl> (nomen) item <bl>deman</bl> (verbum) Teuton: <bl>doemen</bl>.
units.tr: Duom, judgment; duoma, judgments; duomot, judged. These correspond in sound and sense to the Saxon dom, our doome, Teutonic doem (noun), and likewise deman (verb), Teutonic doemen.

units.la: Duomis, Templum] A Latin. Dominicum; & Dominus, de quo pluribus Spelmannus noster in voce Dominicum; nisi malis à domus, quod templum domus sit per excellentiam, Dei scil. ipsius domus. Hîc etiam vide Kilian. verbo Dom. & Befold. de Nat. Pop. cap. 18. in voce Dome.
units.tr: Duomis, temple. From the Latin Dominicum, and Dominus, on which our Spelman writes at length under Dominicum; unless you prefer to derive it from domus, since the temple is the house par excellence, namely God's own house. Here see also Kilian under Dom, and Befold, On the Nature of Peoples, ch. 18, under Dome.

units.la: Verba:
units.tr: Words:

units.la: <bl>Dualont</bl>, Errant: nunc <bl>dolen</bl>] Huic affine Sax: <bl>dpelian</bl>, errare, <bl>zeodpylo</bl>; error, <bl>zeodpola</bl>, & <bl>zeodpolman</bl>; Hæreticus. Conveniunt Belg. <bl>dwaelen</bl>, & <bl>dwaelingbe</bl>, de quibus vid. Kilian.
units.tr: Dualont, to err: now dolen. Akin to this is the Anglo-Saxon dpelian [dwelian], to err; zeodpylo [gedwyla], error; and zeodpola [gedwola] and zeodpolman [gedwolman], a heretic. The Belgic dwaelen and dwaelingbe agree with it; on these see Kilian.

units.la: E
units.tr: E

units.la: <bl>Egisso</bl>, Pavor: <bl>Egisin</bl>, Horroris: <bl>Egisliikis</bl>,
units.tr: Egisso, fear; Egisin, of horror; Egisliikis,

units.la: Ɛgislikts, Terribilis: & Ɛgisliko, Terribiliter: nos Ɛisseltk] Omnes istæ quatuor voces eandem, ut verisimile est, sapiunt originem cum Saxon. ezḝ, timor, & ezḝlic, terribilis, quibus etiam terriculamenta ezḝezṗimma 7 Inde forte Larva eis hazerṗe, hazterṗe, vulgò hodie a bagge.
units.tr: Egislikts, terrible; and Egisliko, terribly. We say Eisseltk. All these four words, as is likely, have the same origin as the Saxon ezḝ, fear, and ezḝlic, terrible, by which the scarecrows are also called. Hence perhaps the word for a mask, hazerpe or hazterpe, commonly today a bagge.

units.la: Ɛdwlt, Opprobrium] Eodem sensu Sax. eopiᵴ, & seopiᵴ, quod ab eorum stᵴpitan fluens, imputare, exprobrare, sonat; unde nostrum twtting, ut alicui in aliquo exprobrare, vulgò dicimus, to twtt one with this of that.
units.tr: Edwlt, reproach. In the same sense the Saxon eopiᵴ and seopiᵴ, which, flowing from their verb stᵴpitan, means to impute or upbraid. Whence our twtting: we commonly say to twit one with this or that.

units.la: Ɛbt, Verò.
units.tr: Ebt, truly.

units.la: Ɛst, Autem.
units.tr: Est, moreover.

units.la: Ɛino, Solus] Hoc Sax. ana, de quo velim consulas Spelmanni nostri Glossar.in voce An.
units.tr: Eino, alone. This is the Saxon ana, on which I would have you consult our Spelman's Glossary under An.

units.la: Ɛinodis, Solitudinis: & Ɛinods, Solitudine] Compositum reor à præcedenti Ɛino, & adjectitiâ particulâ, bod, ut olim scriptum, postea bepd,belt, bat; Sax. haoe, nobis bood, i.e. genus, conditio, qualitas, status, ut pluribus à me alibi ostensum, in Tractatu de Ɛabelkinɒ, nondum edito, cap. 4. Ɛinod itaque statum solitarium signat.
units.tr: Einodis, of solitude; and Einods, in solitude. I think it is compounded from the preceding Eino and the added particle bod, formerly written bod, later bepd, belt, bat. The Saxon haoe, in our word bood, means kind, condition, quality, or status, as I have shown elsewhere at length in my Treatise on Ɛabelkinɒ, not yet published, ch. 4. Einod therefore signifies a solitary state.

units.la: Cintisce, Antiquo : à Latino, ut videtur, ut nos Anttikscbe, & Cntiscen, Antiquis.
units.tr: Cintisce, ancient. From the Latin, as it seems, just as we say Anttikscbe, and Cntiscen, the ancients.

units.la: Cttir, Venenum an Cffer noftrum, id est Pus?] Sax. eodem sensu αττοπ, & Ατταρene.
units.tr: Cttir, poison, or Cffer, our word for pus? In the same sense the Saxon attop and Atterlene.

units.la: Clelendig, Extraneus : & Cllendiga, Advenam : & Clelendis, Peregrinationis] Videatur hîc Kilian. in vocib. Cl-lendo, Cllendigb, & Cl-lendigbepo.
units.tr: Clelendig, foreign; Cllendiga, a stranger; Clelendis, of wandering. See Kilian under Cl-lendo, Cllendigb, and Cl-lendigbepo.

units.la: Cldi, Senecta: & Creldi, Senium. Nam Cr auget] Saxon. senecta, ylop̄e. Senium autem ylopene : unde noftratium Olo, i. e. Senex ; Clder, Senior ; Cldeft, Antiquissimus : Sax. ylopta, alias ealpa eloerto, (non alder-eldeft, ut Versteganus, perperam) quasi omnium senior.
units.tr: Cldi, old age; Creldi, seniority. For the prefix Cr augments the sense. Saxon senecta, ylope; senium, ylopene: whence our Olo, that is, an old man; Clder, an elder; Cldeft, most ancient. The Saxon ylopta, otherwise ealpa eloerto (not alder-eldeft, as Verstegan wrongly has it), as it were the senior of all.

units.la: Crurt, Pavimento : quasi Crt-urif, quòd terram tueatur] Vide Kilian. in voce Cre.
units.tr: Crurt, pavement: as if Crt-urif, because it protects the ground. See Kilian under Cre.

units.la: Creve, Hæreditas] Hoc Sax ynpe, enpe, ynppeaponerre? Belg. Crf, Crf-goed, Crve.
units.tr: Creve, inheritance. For this the Anglo-Saxon has yrfe, erfe, and ynppeaponerre. The Belgic has erf, erfgoed, and erve.

units.la: Ctoa, Lex : & Cton, Lege. vide Cltat Ctoenlart, Legislatorem] Sax.
units.tr: Ctoa, law; and Cton, of the law. See Cltat Ctoenlart, a lawgiver. Saxon.

units.la: Lex, Æ. de quo plura apud Spelmannum nostrum, in voce Ꞔtwa. Videatur etiam Kilian. verb. ꞒꞒ. & Ꞔtwe. Legislator autem Sax. Ælæðenðe; ab Æ. lex, & læðan, ferre.
units.tr: Lex, Æ. On which more in our Spelman under Ꞔtwa. See also Kilian under ꞒꞒ and Ꞔtwe. The lawgiver in Saxon is Ælæðenðe, from Æ., law, and læðan, to bring.

units.la: Ꞔtwethon, Æternum] Vide Kilian. verbo Ꞔeutwe.
units.tr: Ꞔtwethon, eternal. See Kilian under Ꞔeutwe.

units.la: Verba.
units.tr: Words.

units.la: Ꞔbfon, Persequi. Ꞔbfon sal, Persequar. Ꞔbtindon, Persequentibus] Sax. eh̄tan, quod persequi significat, de quo supra in Ꞩbttdon. Sal autem hic, & in pluribus verbis tam præcedentibus quàm sequentibus, nota est verbi futuri temporis, cui respondet & Sax. rceal, & nostrum Ꞩhall, de quo vide Gryphiand.de Weichbild, Saxon.c.38. num.17.
units.tr: Ꞔbfon, to pursue; Ꞔbfon sal, I shall pursue; Ꞔbtindon, pursuing. Saxon ehtan, which means to pursue, on which see above under Ꞩbttdon. Sal here, and in many words both preceding and following, marks the future tense, to which the Saxon rceal corresponds, and our shall. On this see Gryphiander, On the Weichbild, Saxon, ch. 38, n. 17.

units.la: F
units.tr: F

units.la: Facinga, Dormitatio: nos Ꞩaecꞩ. vide Facon.
units.tr: Facinga, Slumber: we say Saec. See Facon.

units.la: Farbiokannost, Prævaricationes.
units.tr: Farbiokannost, Transgressions.

units.la: Fardtuncon, Crapulatus] Sax. hoc opfep-dʒuncon, unde nostrū dzunke, & dzunken, Belg. dzoncken; Teuton. trüncken, eo sensu.
units.tr: Fardtuncon, Drunken. The Old English is ofdruncen, whence our "drunk" and "drunken," Dutch "dronken," German "trunken," in the same sense.

units.la: Farkatha, Abominabilis. Farwathena, Maledicti. Farwatbanuall, Abominatione. Farwet, Abominatus] ropcuꝯ & ꝑnacoo, Saxon. Nequam, Pravus, Vilis, Turpis.
units.tr: Farkatha, Abominable. Farwatha, Cursed. Farwatbanuall, Abomination. Farwet, Abominated. The Saxon words wyrs and wrāc mean worthless, base, vile, foul.

units.la: Farfeggent, Excusandos] Forte à far, Sax.ꝑop, Teut. Aer, pro, & seggben, Sax.ꝑecꝯean, dicere.
units.tr: Farfeggent, To be excused. Perhaps from far, Old English for, meaning "before," and seggan, to say.

units.la: Fattira, Munita] Huic affine Sax, ꝑæꝓtene, ꝑæꝓtnyꝓꝓe, ꝑæꝓtnunꝯe, quæ omnia munitione, municipiu, &c. signant: unde nostrum fast, Teuton. bast, pro firmus; item to fasten, id est, firmare, & simil.
units.tr: Fattira, Fortified. Akin to this are the Saxon fæstene, fæstnysse, and fæstnunge, all meaning fortification, a stronghold, and so on. Whence our "fast," German "fest," meaning firm; likewise "to fasten," that is, to make firm, and the like.

units.la: Farthzoza, Tædio] Saxon.apporeny ꝓꝓe.
units.tr: Farthzoza, Weariness. Saxon, weariness.

units.la: Felts, Rupem] Saxonibus olim & nobis hodieque stints, silices. Vide Kilian.in belt.
units.tr: Felts, Rock. The Saxons formerly, and we today, call flints stints. See Kilian under belt.

units.la: Ferreno, Longè: nos Aerre] Sax. ꝑeoꝓp; nos farre, Germ.ferr.
units.tr: Ferreno, Far off: we say far. Saxon feorran; we say farre, German ferr.

units.la: Ferthe, Excessu] Huic affine nostratium sorth, quod à Sax. ꝑapan, i.e. ire, venit, quibus ꝑopꝓzanꝯ, pro processus; item ꝑopꝓꝓape, pro obitus, vel exitus.
units.tr: Ferthe, Departure. Akin to this is our word "forth," which comes from the Saxon faran, that is, to go. Whence forðgang, for progress, and forðfær, for death or departure.

units.la: Fetberacco, Alarum: nos Aederen] Nos feathers, à Saxon. ꝓyꝯena, id est, alæ, pennæ.
units.tr: Fetberacco, Of wings: we say feathers. Our "feathers" comes from the Saxon fiðera, that is, wings, feathers.

units.la: - sfo,Pecora:nos bee.sfo.Pecuniam. nota sic à pecude, ut Latinis] Saxonibus, pecunia, bona, substantia, ꝓeoh : peçus autem iis ypꝓe, & nÿten? De voce ypꝓe, Freherus, notis in Decalogum, Anglo-Saxonicâ lingua scriptum, præcepto ultimo : » sfe (in- » quit) pecus omne comprehendit, in » quo bovem, asinum. Ethelstani lex, » cap. 1. Be thon the pse befppise ; » i. e. De iis qui pecudem vestigiis per- » sequuntur : ssse autem nil aliud » quàm Erbe, hæreditas, pecunia, » opes. Nec de solis Germanis Ta- » citus ; Pecorum fœcunda, eaque sola » & gratissima opes sunt : sed & de » Hispanis Justinus : Armenta Gery- » onis, quæ illis temporibus sola opes ha- » bebantur. Imo & Romanorum pe- » cunia, unde nisi à pecudibus ?
units.tr: Feoh, Cattle: we say fee. Feoh also means money. The Saxons call money, goods, and substance feoh, but cattle they call wyrð? On the word wyrð, Freher, in his notes on the Decalogue written in Anglo-Saxon, on the last precept, says: "feoh" (he says) comprises all cattle, including ox and ass. Æthelstan's law, chapter 1, reads: "Concerning those who pursue cattle by their tracks." Feoh is nothing other than inheritance, property, money, and wealth. Nor is this true only of the Germans. Tacitus says: "Their wealth is in cattle, the fruitful and the only and most welcome wealth." Justin says the same of the Spaniards: "The herds of Geryon, which in those times were alone regarded as wealth." Even the Roman pecunia, whence else but from pecudes?

units.la: - stloberth; Præclara] Quod præclarum, Sax. beoph, & bpyh, unde nostrum bigbt, eodem sensu: sflo, altera compositi pars, quemadmodum assonat Teutonic. beel; & Germanico bil, ita etiam Sax. sul ; unde nostrum sall, plenus. sflobert, igitur quasi sal-bigbt, h.e. exacè; vel exquisitè, clarus, sive claritatis plenus. Vox sequens, flubtrtbon, ejusdem est originis.
units.tr: Stloberth; Famous. The Old English for famous is beorht and byrht, whence our "bright," in the same sense. The second part, sal, resembles the Teutonic beel and the German bil, and likewise the Saxon sul; whence our "full," meaning full. Sloberth, therefore, is as if sal-bright, that is, exceedingly or exquisitely clear, or full of clarity. The following word, flubtrtbon, is of the same origin.

units.la: Fllofcire, Praeclarus, in his talibus filo, est veel, sive Multum] Quid autem /scire, vide infrà in /scieri.
units.tr: Fllofcire, Renowned. In such words filo means very or much. As to /scire, see below under /scieri.

units.la: Fllobardo, Vehementer] Quasi, ut nostrates vulgò, coll-bardlr.
units.tr: Fllobardo, Vehemently. As our countrymen commonly say, it is as if "coll-bard."

units.la: Fillunga, Flagellum: an quia cutem radit, quasi bitller?] Excoriare, nobis to flep.
units.tr: Fillunga, Whip: is it because it scrapes the skin, as if bitller? To flay the skin is in our language "to flay."

units.la: Fintiare, Tenebrae: Germani hodie.
units.tr: Fintiare, Darkness: the Germans today.

units.la: Foltboja, Dextra; & foltbojon, dextris.
units.tr: Foltboja, Right hand; and foltbojon, with the right hands.

units.la: Freifon, Interitu, & Interitionibus. alibi frotfon] Ulreffer, & treffer, Ger. Sax: Sicamb. (inquit Kilian.) vorare, Anglo-Saxon. pnetenalias pnetan.
units.tr: Freifon, In destruction, and in destructions. Elsewhere frotfon. "Ulreffer" and "treffer" in German; the Saxon is pnetan, elsewhere pnetan. Kilian says the Sicambri meant "to devour."

units.la: Fribof, Atrium: & fritbobo, Atria] Vide Kilian. in voce brpd-bof, ubi Asylum, &c. vertit, quod Sax. pniðrtop, de quo multis Spelmann. nosler in voce fribdol. Sax. hof, domus.
units.tr: Fribof, Court; and fritbobo, courts. See Kilian under the word brpd-bof, where he renders asylum and so on; the Saxon is pniðrtop, on which many writers, Spelman among them, have written. Our form is in fribdol. Saxon hof means house.

units.la: Fremitbojone, Alienigenae: quasi ureemt geboine] Saxon. eodem sensu pnembo, & pnemeo, alias /Elpnemeo; quod ad alteram compositi partem, bozona ; hoc Saxonibus zebopen, nobis bozne, à Sax. bæpan, parere.
units.tr: Fremitbojone, Foreigners: as if from ureemt geboine. The Saxon in the same sense is pnembo and pnemeo, otherwise Ælpnemeo. As for the second part of the compound, bozona: the Saxons have zebopen, we have bozne, from the Saxon bæpan, to bear, that is, to bring forth.

units.la: Frno, Mane : nos Stroech.
units.tr: Frno, Mane: we say stroech.

units.la: Fuetkippon, Compedibus : suprà in Ctppon.
units.tr: Fuetkippon, Shackles: see above under Ctppon.

units.la: Fulitha, Putredo: quasi buplichept, & fulithon, fordibus] Hoc nobis filth, & filthinesse, aliàs fotolnesse, à Sax. fylbe, & fulnepre, eodem sensu: item turpitudo, immunditia ; quemadmodum, pul, id est, immundus, turpis, nobis hodie fotole.
units.tr: Fulitha, Rottenness: as if buplichept; and fulithon, filth. To us this is "filth" and "filthinesse," otherwise "fotolnesse," from the Saxon fylþe and fulnyss, in the same sense; also foulness and uncleanness. Just as pul, that is, unclean, foul, is today "foul" with us.

units.la: Fulletbon, Abundantia] Nobis hoc folnesse, à Sax. pullnyrre, plenitudo, copia, abundantia.
units.tr: Fulletbon, Abundance. To us this is "folnesse," from the Saxon pullnyrre, meaning fullness, plenty, abundance.

units.la: Fuotscamel, Scabellum] Hoc Sax. rcamul, rcæmol, rcamel, & potrcamul: à pot, nobis hodie coof, pes, & rcamul, scamnum, scabellum. Hinc scabellum mercatorium, Sax. ceapscamel; Publicanorum, tolscamule ; Campsorum, mynetepa rceamelar; Pulpitum, peadinz rceamle. Hinc etiam Lanionum, Piscatorum, & similium Scabella, nobis hodie shambles dicta. Plura vide apud Kilian. in voce schaemel.
units.tr: Fuotscamel, Footstool. The Saxon is scamul, scæmol, scamel, and potscamul: from pot, which we now call "foot," and scamul, a stool or bench. Hence a market stool, Saxon ceapscamel; of the tax collectors, tolscamule; of the money changers, mynetepa scēamelar; a pulpit, peadinz scēamle. Hence also the stalls of butchers, fishermen, and the like, now called "shambles." More may be seen in Kilian under schaemel.

units.la: Futhon, Auftro] Annon rectius fu-thon ? Sax. enim Auster, buh, & buh-dale, sæle, unde nostrum South. Belg. etiam Auster Sapden-wotnd: Germ. Sud-wotnt.
units.tr: Futhon, South. Would futhon not be more correct? The Saxon for the south wind is suð, and suðdæle, whence our "South." The Dutch also say Suyden-wint for the south wind; German Sud-wind.

units.la: Fullast, Adjutorium: vide follet-sten.
units.tr: Fullast, Help: see follet-sten.

units.la: Farlt, Princeps: & forlstingo, præpositione: nos wɔzst] Ab eâdem origine nostratium stst, (adjectivum) Primus, & adverb. stst, primùm, vel in primis. Plura vide apud Cl. Selden. nostr. Tit. Honor. par. 2. cap. 1. §. 53. & Versteg. cap. 10.
units.tr: Farlt, Prince; and forlstingo, a preposition: we say "first." From the same origin come our "first," as adjective (Primus), and the adverb "first," meaning at first or chiefly. More may be seen in the learned Selden, Titles of Honour, part 2, chapter 1, §53, and in Verstegan, chapter 10.

units.la: Furtteltin, Prodigium: nos wɔzs-tecken] Hoc Sax. pope tacn, & pope beacn. A priori, nostrum tozetoken, voce compositâ à pope, præ, & tacn, nobis token, signum.
units.tr: Furtteltin, Prodigy: we say "wonder-token." The Saxon is fore tacn and fore beacn. Presumably our "foretoken," a compound of fore, before, and tacn, which in our language is "token," a sign.

units.la: Verba.
units.tr: Words.

units.la: Facon-sal, Dormitabit: facodon, dormitaverunt.
units.tr: Facon-sal, He will sleep: facodon, they slept.

units.la: Farlifbon, Transierunt: farlief, transeat] Transire, Sax. papan: unde fare in nostratium twarre-fare, Saxon. pynopape, alias utpape, id est, expeditio. Hinc etiam viatorem vocamus Map-farting-man, Sax. pezpepenb: Mari versatum, ut Nautam, sea-farting-man: mau: fed & maris transfretationem,& aquá trajectum, cum naulo, (Germanis fabzgelt) fare dicimus. Iter autem Sax. fæp: Itinerarium fonboc: quasi itineris codex. Sed & oseplibaN,Sax. transire sonat.
units.tr: Farlifbon, They passed over: farlief, let him pass. To pass over is Saxon faran, whence "fare" in our word "wayfare," that is, an expedition. Hence we also call a traveller a "sea-faring man," as one versed in the sea, a sailor; and we say "fare" both for a crossing of the sea or a water passage and for the ferry payment (Germans Fährgeld). The Saxon for journey is faer, and an itinerary is fonboc, as if to say a "book of the journey." The Saxon word also means to cross over.

units.la: Farbelgeda,Exacerbavit. Vide Belgan, & Irbelgien] Exacerbare, Sax. abilzian. Vide supra Abalgs.
units.tr: Farbelgeda, He exasperated. See Belgan and Irbelgien. To exasperate is Saxon abilzian. See Abalgs above.

units.la: Farstbt, Expugna] Expugnare,Sax. osepseohtan; ab osep,super, nobis ober, & seohtan, German. fechten, Belg. becbsen, pugnare, quasi pugnando vincere, cui bene respondet verbum nostrum to obercome.
units.tr: Farstbt, Take by storm. To take by storm (expugnare) is Saxon ofersēohtan, from ofer, over, our "over" (ober), and seohtan, German fechten, Dutch vechten, to fight; as if to conquer by fighting. Our word "overcome" corresponds well to this.

units.la: Fardilligo, Dele: nos berdilgen] Hoc Saxon, sopoilizan, & aoilzian; unde (forte) eorum oyhle, oizle, & oizhle, pro secretus, ut & oizolhnyrre pro Latibulum.
units.tr: Fardilligo, Destroy: we say <bl>berdilgen</bl>. This is Saxon adilgian and ādilgian, whence perhaps their oyhle, oizle, and oizhle, for secret, as also oizolhnyrre for hiding-place.

units.la: Fartwellunt,Prophanaverunt. Vide Biwellan.
units.tr: Fartwellunt, They profaned. See Biwellan.

units.la: Farschtfan,Concidet,media longa.
units.tr: Farschtfan, He will fall; the middle syllable is long.

units.la: Farnossan wartban sal, Confumitur] Quasi dicas, nullius erit pretii: nossan enim, nullum, wartban, pretium,ut opinor, signat. sal autem, (ut antea monitum) nota verbi futuri tem-
units.tr: Farnossan wartban sal, It will be consumed. As if you were to say, it will be of no value: nossan means nothing, and wartban, as I think, means value. Sal, as noted before, is the sign of the future tense.

units.la: poris: nisi quis malit <bl>wurthan</bl> hic idem sonare ac Sax. ʒepopȯen, id est, fieri: tunc autem verba sonant, adnihilabitur, sive, ad nihilum reducetur.
units.tr: Unless one prefers to take <bl>wurthan</bl> here as having the same sense as Saxon geweorðan, that is, to become. Then the words mean "it will be brought to nothing," or "reduced to nothing."

units.la: Fellon sal, Destruet: nos vellen dejiciet] Eodem sensu (proftrandi scil. sive dejiciendi) nobis to fell, ut in arbore proftrandâ, quod nobis to fell a tree, in bove malleo lanii prostrato, quod nobis felling an ore, & id genus aliis. Fluit autem à verbo faelen, cadere; quod enim sic dejicitur aut destruitur, non sine casu destruitur.
units.tr: Fellon sal, He will destroy: we say vellen, he will throw down. In the same sense (that is, of felling or throwing down) we say to fell, as of a tree that is felled, to fell a tree; of an ox struck down by the butcher's mallet, felling an ox; and so on with other examples. It derives from the verb faelen, to fall; for what is thus cast down or destroyed is destroyed not without a fall.

units.la: Ferterron sal, Perdes: nos verde- ruen: fertherttbu, perdas.
units.tr: Ferterron sal, You will perish: we say verderuen; fertherttbu, that you may perish.

units.la: Fertwerthan sal, Peribit: fertwerthet, Pereatis] Perire Sax. fopnpy̆n̆san.
units.tr: Fertwerthan sal, He will perish; fertwerthet, you shall perish. To perish is Saxon forweorðan.

units.la: Follelcten, Opitulentur] Adjuvare, opem ferre, Sax. fyl̆rtian, unde fultum pro adjutorium.
units.tr: Follelcten, They help. To help, to bring aid, is Saxon fyltian, whence fultum for help.

units.la: Fozsuoz, Prodiit] Huic affine nostratium fozth-fare, quod (ortu Saxonicum) & obitum, & corporis de loco obitus exportationem, funeris ergo, olim signabat.
units.tr: Fozsuoz, He came forth. Akin to this is our forth-fare, which (of Saxon origin) also signified death, and the carrying of a body out from the place of death, and so in former times a funeral.

units.la: Framsozitthu, Recessisti] Compositum reor à fram, nobis hodie from, Sax. autem fpam, i. e. à, ab, & faran, ire, transfire, tranfire, cedere, vide farlitlhan fuprà.
units.tr: Framsozitthu, You withdrew. I think it is compounded of fram, now our "from" (Saxon fram, that is, from, away from), and faran, to go, pass over, depart, yield. See farlitlhan above.

units.la: Framgentan, Declinare] Compofitum videtur à fram, de, vel à, & gangen, vadere, ire, proficisci : unde Ambarvalia Sax. ganzoazar.
units.tr: Framgentan, To turn aside. It seems to be compounded of fram, from or away, and gangen, to walk, go, set out; whence the Saxon gangdagas, the Rogation days (Ambarvalia).

units.la: Framgeletoon, Abduxerunt] Hæc etiam eft vox compofita ; cujus pars posterior ( prior enim ex prætmiffis patet) ejufdem videtur originis ac Saxon. læoan, unde noftrum to lead (verbum) ducere, & Leader (nomen) Dux; Du- ctor.
units.tr: Framgeletoon, They led away. This is also a compound word. Its latter part (the former being clear from what has gone before) seems to be of the same origin as Saxon lǣdan, whence our verb "to lead," meaning to conduct, and the noun "leader," meaning a guide or conductor.

units.la: G.
units.tr: G.

units.la: Gajentwerde, Confpectu : & alibi gajentwajerde, & gentwert] Adverfus, contra, Sax. tozeaner, unde za him tozeaneṛ, i.e. Ito ei obviam, vulgò, goe meet bim. Eodem fenfu eis onzeanꝫ Altera compofiti pars, twerd, nobis hodie tward, ut in towarb, id eft, juxta, prope, &c.
units.tr: Gajentwerde, In the presence of (and elsewhere gajentwajerde, and gentwert): against, opposite; Saxon ongean, whence za him tozeaner, that is, to him on the way, commonly "go meet him." In the same sense, eis onzeanꝫ. The other part of the compound, twerd, is our present "toward," as in "towards," that is, near, close by.

units.la: Garo, Paratus : & garu, idem] Hoc Saxon. zeappe, & zeapu, à zeappian, parare, ornare, præparare ; zeapcunz, præparatio. Teuton. etiam, præparare, gaerwen ; apparare, gaer-maecken.
units.tr: Garo, Ready; and garu, the same. Here Saxon gearo and geara, from gearwian, to prepare, adorn, make ready; gearcung, preparation. The Teutonic also has gaerwen, to prepare, and gaer-maecken, to make ready.

units.la: Galenderl, Incantantis] Talis, Sax. zaleno, & onzaleno.
units.tr: Galenderl, Of an enchanter: such a one is Saxon galdor and ongaldor.

units.la: Hoc Teuton. gaertoe, garbe, Gallis gerbe, Latino-barbaris garba: nec longè abit Sax. ʒnipe, unde nostrum grtpe, eâdem notione.
units.tr: Here Teutonic gaertoe, garbe; Gallic gerbe; Latin-barbarous garba. Nor is far from these the Saxon gripe, whence our grype (a grip), with the same meaning.

units.la: Hoc Saxon. ʒeopeẹeo, & ʒeopeḥtz.
units.tr: Here Saxon geopeo and geopeht.

units.la: Vide Cl. Spelman. in voce Ber-glum.
units.tr: See the learned Spelman under the word <bl>Ber-glum</bl>.

units.la: Sculptile, Sax. ʒnapen, nobis hodie graben, quemadmodum statua nobis vulgò a graben image.
units.tr: Sculptile: Saxon grafen, whence our "graven," as a statue is commonly called a <bl>graven image</bl>.

units.la: Hoc Sax.onʒepnemeo, & unʒepnemeo ; voce composita à negandi five privandi particula, on,un, i.e. non,& ʒepne-meo, perfectus.
units.tr: Here Saxon ungemeo and unġemeo, a compound of the negative or privative particle on or un, that is, not, and gemeo, perfect.

units.la: Meretrix Saxon. hope,nobis (to, voci perperam præponentibus)toboze : perperam dico; nam ab hypan venit, i.e.precio conducere, quod vox etiam Latina sat plane confirmat.
units.tr: Harlot: Saxon hore, which we now call <bl>whore</bl> (wrongly placing "to" before the word). I say wrongly, for it comes from hyran, that is, to hire for a price, which the Latin word also quite plainly confirms.

units.la: Sax. confensus zeleafe, & leafniȷ, unde nostrum, eodem sensu, <bl>leatbe</bl>, i.e. licentia, quod Belg. <bl>Dozlof, bet-lof</bl>. Germ. <bl>Erlaab, Erlaubnus</bl>.
units.tr: Saxon for consent is geleafe and leafnis, whence our <bl>leave</bl>, in the same sense, that is, permission. The Dutch say <bl>Oorlof</bl>, <bl>verlof</bl>; the Germans <bl>Erlaab</bl>, <bl>Erlaubnis</bl>.

units.la: <bl>Bellboze</bl>, Libera] Hoc, ut & nostrum <bl>dellber</bl>, latinizant.
units.tr: <bl>Bellboze</bl>, Free. This, like our <bl>deliver</bl>, they put into Latin.

units.la: <bl>Delibedelit</bl>, Deprecabilis] Saxon. biodan, est orare, rogare, precari, cujus (ni fallor) in hac voce quale quale vestigium.
units.tr: <bl>Delibedelit</bl>, Prayable (deprecabilis). Saxon biddan means to pray, ask, or entreat; some trace of which, unless I am mistaken, remains in this word.

units.la: <bl>Belende</bl>, Accola. Vide <bl>Elelendige</bl>.
units.tr: <bl>Belende</bl>, Dweller. See <bl>Elelendige</bl>.

units.la: <bl>Gemerka</bl>, Terminus] Finis, terminus Sax. zemaṗne. unde hodie agrorum fines sive limites <bl>metres</bl>, alias <bl>meers</bl>, vocamus. <bl>Mark</bl> alias <bl>meart</bl>, & <bl>mareb</bl>, eodem sensu utimur.
units.tr: <bl>Gemerka</bl>, Boundary: end, limit; Saxon gemaere. Whence today we call the boundaries or limits of fields <bl>metres</bl>, otherwise <bl>meers</bl>. We use <bl>mark</bl>, otherwise <bl>meart</bl> and <bl>mareb</bl>, in the same sense.

units.la: <bl>Gibert</bl>, Libera. vide <bl>gebere</bl>] Hoc Sax. zeṗṗéo, ab eorum zeṗṗean, Belg. <bl>brpen</bl>, Teut. frejen, liberare, quo sensu nostrum to free, vel set free.
units.tr: <bl>Gibert</bl>, Free. See <bl>gebere</bl>. Saxon gefreogan, from their gefreo, Dutch <bl>vrijen</bl>, Teutonic freyen, to free; in which sense we say <bl>to free</bl>, or <bl>set free</bl>.

units.la: <bl>Genubte</bl>, Abundantia: ab eo quod nos genoech, satis. vide genubtegot. <bl>Genubt samozt</bl>, Uberi] Copia, abundantia, Sax. zeniþtrumnyrye ? Satis autem zenoþ, unde nostrum enough. Hinc uber (adject.) Sax. zeniþtrum i casu ablat. zenithtrumpe ?
units.tr: <bl>Genubte</bl>, Abundance; from which we get <bl>genoech</bl>, enough. See <bl>genubtegot</bl>. <bl>Genubt samozt</bl>, Rich: plenty, abundance; Saxon genyhtsumnes? Enough is Saxon genoh, whence our "enough." Hence uber (adjective), Saxon genyhtsum, in the ablative case.

units.la: <bl>Begualbit</bl>, Coagulatus: vide <bl>Betw-allit</bl>. <bl>Gerigt</bl>
units.tr: <bl>Begualbit</bl>, Coagulated: see <bl>Betw-allit</bl>. <bl>Gerigt</bl>.

units.la: {a}Gerlbtnaffis, Refectionis] Non multum abit à Saxon. ʒeꝑ eoponyƿƿe, illo senfu accepto.
units.tr: <bl>Gerlbtnaffis</bl>, Of refreshment: not far from the Saxon word for refreshment, taken in that sense.

units.la: {b}Gesceudɒt, Confufi] Hoc Saxon. ʒeꝛcynꝺe, ut & dedecus eis ꝑconꝺe. Hinc forte nostratium ꝺhent, & ꝺhen-ꝺing, (ge, particula verborum præteritis, & participiis præteriti temporis apud Saxones & Germanos præposita, hic omissa) quæ proprie increpationem notat: ab increpatione autem oritur confusio. Vide Verstegan.verb.scende, & Kilian. in schanꝺe.
units.tr: <bl>Gesceudɒt</bl>, Confused: Saxon gescynde, as also dedecus (disgrace) eis ꝑconꝺe. Hence perhaps the Dutch <bl>dhent</bl> and <bl>dhen-ding</bl>, where ge, a particle placed before verbs in the past tense and before participles among the Saxons and Germans, is omitted here. This properly denotes reproach, and confusion arises from reproach. See Verstegan, under scende, and Kilian, under <bl>schande</bl>.

units.la: {c}Gefigenero Inclinato.
units.tr: <bl>Gefigenero</bl>, Inclined.

units.la: {d}Gesisse, Visione] Hoc Sax. ʒeƿƿe, ab eorum ʒeƿeon fluens, quod videre sonat. Visio autem & Visus nobis hodie sight.
units.tr: <bl>Gesisse</bl>, Vision: Saxon gesihþe, flowing from their gesēon, which means to see. We now call vision and sight by the name "sight."

units.la: {e}Gefcatbot, Condemnatus: an proprie Mulctatus?] Vide Scatban sal.
units.tr: <bl>Gefcatbot</bl>, Condemned: or properly fined? See <bl>Scatban sal</bl>.

units.la: {f}Getelt, Tentoria] Hoc Sax. ʒeƿelꝺ; unde nostrum Tilt pro Tentorio.
units.tr: <bl>Getelt</bl>, Tents: Saxon gesceld; whence our "tilt" for tent.

units.la: {g}Getuugel, Linguosus] Talis Sax. ʒeƿinʒe, & ƿunʒƿull; quibus Eloquentia ʒeƿinʒneƿƿe; Lingua; ƿonʒa; ƿunʒel autem iis, astrum, planeta, syꝺus: ƿunʒelcnæpƿ, Astronomia, &c.
units.tr: <bl>Getuugel</bl>, Talkative: such a one is Saxon gewinge and wunsull; to these belong eloquence (gewinnenes), tongue (wunga). Wunzel, however, means star, planet, sidus; wunzelcnæpt, astronomy, and so on.

units.la: {h}Getawtng, Disciplina] Mos, ritus, Saxon. ȝeþeape, alias ȝeþÿpe.
units.tr: <bl>Getawtng</bl>, Discipline: custom, rite; Saxon geþeaw, otherwise geþyþe.

units.la: Getunkt,Pactum] Conditio,Saxon. ȝeᴛincȝe, & ȝeᴅinȝ; pacifci,ȝeᴅinȝian.
units.tr: <bl>Getunkt</bl>, Pact: condition; Saxon getinge and gedinc; to make a pact, gedingian.

units.la: Gebertbe, Iter. vide Aertbe.
units.tr: <bl>Gebertbe</bl>, Journey. See <bl>Aertbe</bl>.

units.la: Gebvede, Veftimenta] Vide Waf.
units.tr: <bl>Gebvede</bl>, Garments. See <bl>Waf</bl>.

units.la: Gebvefanuftt,Subftantia: & getwin, poffeffio; getwnt idem] Poffeffio,Sax. ȝepinn, ab eorum ȝepinnan fluens, Teuton. ghewinnen, nancifci, acquirere, obtinere, &c. unde noftrum to winne, (verbum) item winning, (nomen.)
units.tr: Gebvefanuftt, Substance; and getwin, possession; getwnt the same. Possession: Saxon gewinn, flowing from their gewinnan; Teutonic ghewinnen, to get, acquire, obtain. Whence our verb to win and the noun winning.

units.la: Getwitt, Scientia] Hoc Saxon.pitᴞ, & ȝepiᴛᴞ, quorum prius nobis manfit.
units.tr: <bl>Getwitt</bl>, Knowledge: Saxon gewit, and gewite, of which the former has remained with us.

units.la: Getwitfcopt, Teftimonia] Hoc Sax. ȝepiᴛnyrrȝa, unde noftrum twitnefte, pro teftimonio. Sax. etiam,teftium ftipatio, ȝepiᴛᴞcype.
units.tr: <bl>Getwitfcopt</bl>, Testimonies: Saxon gewitnesse, whence our <bl>witness</bl> for testimony. The Saxons also had gewitnescype for a gathering of witnesses.

units.la: Getwifto,Etenim,Enim]Certus,Sax. ȝepir : porrò, ȝepirlice.
units.tr: <bl>Getwifto</bl>, Indeed; for: certain; Saxon gewis; moreover, gewislice.

units.la: Gtverfunthedon, Opportunitatibus.
units.tr: <bl>Gtverfunthedon</bl>, Opportunities.

units.la: Gipondt, Patens: nos gapende forte] Anglis gaping', à Saxon.ȝeopnian, aperire. Patens etiam eis opnienoe, & opnizenoe, unde noftratium open, & openting, illo fenfu.
units.tr: <bl>Gipondt</bl>, Open: we perhaps say <bl>gaping</bl>, from the Saxon geopnian, to open. Open in Saxon is opnienoe and opnizenoe, whence our <bl>open</bl> and <bl>opening</bl>, in that sense.

units.la: Hoc Sax. ȝeħaȼ, & beħaȼ, unde bebigbt in Psalterio nostro metrico (ut vocant) sæpius obvium, eo sensu. Sax. beħeħȼ.
units.tr: Here Saxon gehæg, and behæg, whence <bl>bebigbt</bl> in our metrical Psalter (as they call it), frequently met with, in that sense. Saxon behæg.

units.la: Prudens Sax. ȝleap. Legum etiam periti eis Æȝleāpan dicti, ab eorum Æ, Lex, & eodem ȝleap, peritus.
units.tr: Prudent: Saxon gleaw. Those learned in the laws were also called Ægleapan, from their Æ, law, and the same gleap, skilled.

units.la: Mos, Ritus, Sax. ȝeȏȳpe, aliās ȝeȏeap?
units.tr: Custom, rite: Saxon gewyrpe, otherwise geweorp?

units.la: Sax. arma, pæpn, unde nostrum eodem sensu, weapon. Hoc Belg. wapen: Germ. waffen.
units.tr: Arms: Saxon wæpn, whence our <bl>weapon</bl> in the same sense. Dutch <bl>wapen</bl>; German <bl>Waffen</bl>.

units.la: Pœna, tor-tura, mulĉta, Saxon. pıȝe; Tortores, pıȝenepeȝ; punire, pıȝnian?
units.tr: Punishment, torture, fine: Saxon pine. Torturers: pinepeg; to punish: pinian?

units.la: Lubricum Sax. ȝlio, unde nostratium to glide & glidung, eo sensu. Hinc forte Milvus, Sax. ȝlioa dictus.
units.tr: Slippery: Saxon gliō, whence our words <bl>to glide</bl> and <bl>glidung</bl>, in that sense. Hence perhaps the kite (milvus) was called in Saxon glioa.

units.la: Cogitatio, Saxon. ȝeȏohȝ, unde nostratium thought, illo sensu.
units.tr: Thought: Saxon gehoht, whence our <bl>thought</bl>, in that sense.

units.la: Ejusdem (forte) originis ac nostrūm
units.tr: Perhaps of the same origin as our

units.la: G g 2
units.tr: G g 2

units.la: nostrum grabe, Belg. graf & grabe, sepulchrum. Lucus etiam nobis grobe, de quo Spelman. noster, in voce graba.
units.tr: our <bl>grave</bl>, Dutch <bl>graf</bl> and <bl>grabe</bl>, sepulchre. Also <bl>grobe</bl>, a grove, our word, concerning which see Spelman under graba.

units.la: Gnollihe, & gnlltke, Gloria : & alibi gnoltchetne. vide gnoltcan] Sax. puloop, & pulope, gloria, pulooplic, gloriofus.
units.tr: <bl>Gnollihe</bl> and <bl>gnlltke</bl>, Glory: and elsewhere <bl>gnoltchetne</bl>; see <bl>gnoltcan</bl>. Saxon wuldor and wuldor, glory; wuldorlic, glorious.

units.la: Verba.
units.tr: Words.

units.la: Gebaltbon, Irritaverunt. vide Balgon] Belgon potius, & Abalgt.
units.tr: Gebaltbon, They have provoked. See Balgon; perhaps rather Belgon, and Abalgt.

units.la: Gebzedtwertbtt, Fundatur.
units.tr: Gebzedtwertbtt, It is founded.

units.la: Geberfoes, Coronafti : Et alibi gerinlf, coronat, itemque gereboffo, coronafti] Vide supra garo.
units.tr: Geberfoes, Thou hast crowned; and elsewhere gerinlf, he crowns, likewise gereboffo, thou hast crowned. See above garo.

units.la: Gebirmon, quiescere : gebirmeba, quievit : gebirme, quiescam. Ungebirmlich, Incessabilis.
units.tr: Gebirmon, to rest; gebirmeba, he rested; gebirme, I shall rest. Ungebirmlich, unceasing.

units.la: Gelicoba, Complacui. vide Lfcont] Complacere, Sax. zelicean : nobis hodie to lihe : complacui autem, eis ic zelicoba ; nobis hodie 3 lkeb.
units.tr: Gelicoba, I was pleasing. See Lfcont. To please is in Saxon zelicean, which we today render "to like"; "I pleased" is in Saxon ic zelicoba, which we today render "I liked".

units.la: Gefuogan, Adjicies] Saxon. foz, & zefoz item foozinz, Junctura, conjunctio.
units.tr: Gefuogan, Thou wilt add. Saxon foz, and zefoz; likewise foozinz, a joining, a conjunction.

units.la: Getobotoliban, Obriguerunt] Priori vocis parti affine nostratium tonab, Sax. toh, id est, tenax, lentus, quibus lentum vimen, tohzaepo ?
units.tr: Getobotoliban, They became stiff. The first part of the word is akin to our tonab; Saxon toh, that is, tough, pliant, whence tohzaepo (?), a tough osier.

units.la: Gemnfof,
units.tr: Gemnfof,

units.la: <bl>Gemafos</bl>,Mutabis.
units.tr: Gemafos, Thou shalt change.

units.la: <bl>Gemetnt</bl>,Communicabo] Communis, Sax. <bl>ʒemæne</bl>,unde nostrum <bl>Peo-</bl> <bl>men</bl>, vulgus, Belg. <bl>Wolck gbemeypte</bl>, Germ. <bl>Das gemepn Doclk</bl>.Hinc etiam Pascuum commune, Cantianis nostris <bl>Spenps</bl>,& <bl>Spinis</bl>, quasi <bl>ʒemænnyr</bl>,id est,Communitatis, vulgò <bl>the Spanpes</bl>.
units.tr: Gemetnt, I will communicate. Common, Saxon gemæne, whence our "commen", the common people; Dutch "gemeyne", German "das gemein Volk". Hence also pasture held in common, which our Kentish men call "Spanps" and "Spinis", as if gemænnyr, that is, of community, commonly "the Spanpes".

units.la: Gtbert; Libera, Imperandi] De hoc & duobus proximè sequentibus verbis, gtbereda, & geberan sal, vide Gtbert, supra, inter Nomina.
units.tr: Gtbert; free, of commanding. On this and the two following words, gtbereda and geberan sal, see Gtbert above, among the nouns.

units.la: <bl>Genabtegod</bl>, Abundavit. Vide <bl>genabte</bl>.
units.tr: Genabtegod, He abounded. See genabte.

units.la: <bl>Geocodon</bl>,Abdiderunt] Rectiùs forsan Addiderunt. Addere autem Saxon: <bl>ʒeiccan</bl>, aliàs <bl>ʒeeacan</bl>, unde nostrum <bl>eeked</bl>, additus,adjectus,uti & <bl>eke</bl>, pro etiam.
units.tr: Geocodon, They put away; perhaps rather "they added". Saxon ʒeiccan, otherwise ʒeeacan, whence our "eeked", added, adjected; as also "eke", meaning also.

units.la: <bl>Gequicco</bl>,Vivifica] Vivus,Sax. cuc, unde nostrum <bl>quick</bl>, eopse sensu; ramcucene, eis semi-mortuus. Vivificare autem nobis hodie <bl>to quicken</bl>. Hinc autem verbum hîc sequens <bl>gequicceda</bl>, vivificet.
units.tr: Gequicco, Quicken thou. Living, Saxon cuc, whence our "quick", in the same sense; ramcucene, as semi-dead. To quicken, as we say today, is "to quicken". Hence the following verb gequicceda, let him quicken.

units.la: <bl>Gerwon</bl>,Parare : <bl>tbu gerwodes</bl>,parafti : <bl>gerwon sal</bl>, parabit : <bl>gerwodon</bl>, paraverunt: <bl>gerwindod</bl>, præparans: <bl>gerwida</bl>, gerwida, paravi.: gegertwef, præparabitur] Vide supra Garo.
units.tr: Gerwon, to prepare: tbu gerwodes, thou hast prepared; gerwon sal, he will prepare; gerwodon, they prepared; gerwindod, preparing; gerwida, gerwida, I prepared; gegertwef, will be prepared. See above Garo.

units.la: Gelpurt Dos, Investigasti] Investigare, Sax. berpÿnian.; vestigium ꝓpon. Teuton. hodie, Investigatio gbelpoze. Kilian. [illegible, ~8 letters]
units.tr: Gelpurt Dos, Thou hast searched out. To investigate, Saxon berpÿnian; a footprint, ꝓpon. Teutonic today, investigation gbelpoze. Kilian. [illegible, about eight letters]

units.la: Getimbzlt, Ædificabitur] Ædifica-re, Sax. ꝝetumbhian, Belg. timmeren, German. stimmeren: unde nostratium timber. Belg. timmerbont, German. zimmer, i.e. tignum, lignum, voce autem Latino-barbarâ, mærenhium, de quâ D. Watsius in Glossar.
units.tr: Getimbzlt, Shall be built. To build, Saxon ꝝetumbhian, Dutch timmeren, German stimmeren; whence our "timber"; Dutch timmerbont, German zimmer, that is, timber or log. But there is also a Latin-barbarous word, mærenhium, on which see D. Watsius in the Glossary.

units.la: Getrimbetos, Fabricatus] Formare, imò & stabilire, Sax. ꝝetumman: à priori, nostrum trim, E. G. trith and trim, i.e. elegans & perpolitus; qualis qui sub manibus barbitonsoris fuerit, cujus opificium, nobis trimming dictum. Plura videinfrà in Sanctreft.
units.tr: Getrimbetos, Made. To form, indeed also to establish, Saxon ꝝetumman. From the former comes our "trim", as in "trith and trim", that is, elegant and polished; such as one who has been under the barber's hands, whose trade we call "trimming". More below, under Sanctreft.

units.la: Gefocon, Adjiciam: supra gefuogan] Vide Geoto on supra.
units.tr: Gefocon, I will add: see above gefuogan. See Geoto above.

units.la: Getweigit, Vexatus] Sax. pap, nobis hodie woh, dolor, huic verbo inest, ut mihi persuasum.
units.tr: Getweigit, Vexed. Saxon pap; we today say woh, pain. I am persuaded that this word has something of that sense.

units.la: Getopt, Benedictus: & geldpungə, benedictio.
units.tr: Getopt, Blessed: and geldpungə, blessing.

units.la: Gebinsos, Visitas] Sax. visitare zeneoran? Gtoolot,
units.tr: Gebinsos, Thou visitest. Saxon visitare zeneoran? Gtoolot,

units.la: @Gibolof, alias gittalof, superbit.
units.tr: Gibolof, alias gittalof, is proud.

units.la: @Gemacoda, Concinnabat] Affine nostratium to make, à Sax. ȝemacian, facere.
units.tr: Gemacoda, He was arranging. Akin to our to make, from Saxon ȝemacian, to make.

units.la: @Ginroda, Genuit.
units.tr: Ginroda, He begot.

units.la: @Geminsoda, Diminuit] Diminutio, Saxonibus minyunȝ, nobis mincing: ut cibus frustatim, & minutim concifus, nobis mincedmeat, alias mincemeat.
units.tr: Geminsoda, He diminishes. Diminution: Saxon minyunȝ, for us mincing, as food cut up into small pieces and minced is for us mincedmeat, otherwise mincemeat.

units.la: @Segiroda, Paravit] Superiùs ad @Giʒo notatis, hîc adde, quòd vestimentum, amictus, Saxonibus ȝyplan, ȝeȝyplan; unde eis mnunc ȝeȝyplan, pro habitu, sive apparatu monachico, Bedæ, Caracalla: item vestimenta ecclesiastica, eis cyncean, ȝeȝynela; @Geare, etiam in Scotorum @Gaoes & @Geare, pro bonis & supelleƈtile, quemadmodum in nostratium nigbtgeare, bead-geare, id est, nocturnali, capitali, apparatu, huc, ni fallor, referendum.
units.tr: Segiroda, He prepared. Above, at the words noted under @Giʒo, add here that clothing or dress is in Saxon ȝyplan, ȝeȝyplan; whence now ȝeȝyplan for monastic habit or equipment, in Bede, Caracalla; likewise ecclesiastical vestments, cyncean, ȝeȝynela. Geare, also in Scottish Gaoes and Geare, means goods and household furniture, as in our nightgeare and bead-geare, that is, nocturnal and head equipment, which, unless I am mistaken, is to be referred here.

units.la: @Gimarsaba, Mirificavit. Vide @Gomarda] Magnificare, Saxonibus mæprian;
units.tr: Gimarsaba, He magnified. See Gomarda. To magnify, Saxon mæprian.

units.la: @Gssatundon, Acceleraverunt] Citò, confestim, Sax. pona, nobis soone.
units.tr: Gssatundon, They hastened. Quickly, at once: Saxon pona, for us "soone".

units.la: @Gt-
units.tr: Gt-

units.la: Gimtklloda, Magnificabimur. Vide Piktil.
units.tr: Gimtklloda, We shall be magnified. See Piktil.

units.la: Gibzeftt, Defit.
units.tr: Gibzeftt, He lacks.

units.la: Gferbun sal, Hæreditabit] Hinc Teutonicis Erben, i.e. hæreditate accipere bona, quod Sax. ypfpeapoian; ut hæres eis ypfenuma. Vide supra Ereve.
units.tr: Gferbun sal, He will inherit. Hence the Teutonic Erben, that is, to receive goods by inheritance, which is Saxon ypfpeapoian; as heir is eis ypfenuma. See above Ereve.

units.la: Gitatodon, Locaverunt] Locus, sedes, Sax. ptyoe & pteo, quod nobis manet, cum in villarum quamplurium denominationibus, ita terminantibus, cujusmodi (in agro Cantiano) Berteed, Pilkteed, Frenteed, Elmeteed, Linteed, & simil. tum inter loquendum, ut cum dicimus, in the stead of another, id est, loco alterius, quomodo etiam Teutonicis usurpatur.
units.tr: Gitatodon, They placed. Place, seat: Saxon ptyoe and pteo, which remains with us in the names of many villages ending thus, such as (in the Kentish country) Berteed, Pilkteed, Frenteed, Elmeteed, Linteed, and the like. It is also used in speech, as when we say "in the stead of another", that is, in the place of another, as the Teutonics also use it.

units.la: Gtet, Confitetur. Vide Begibte.
units.tr: Gtet, He confesses. See Begibte.

units.la: Gifcargidt, Expulisti. Vide Belcargt] Et Scargt.
units.tr: Gifcargidt, Thou hast expelled. See Belcargt; and Scargt.

units.la: Gomarda, Mirificavit, a Par, Fama] Vide supra Gimarsada.
units.tr: Gomarda, He magnified, from Par, fame. See above Gimarsada.

units.la: Goomawirtitnt, Epulentur.
units.tr: Goomawirtitnt, They feast.

units.la: Gnolican sal, Glorificabo: & gnolican sulint, glorificabunt] Vide gnoltke.
units.tr: Gnolican sal, I will glorify: and gnolican sulint, they will glorify. See gnoltke.

units.la: H
units.tr: H

units.la: Hasta, Captivitas. In Ubiis hodie, ita Carcer] Corrigendum forte hasta, Sax. enim, Captivitas ἁαρτυnunʒe, & ἁαρτynýoε.Captivus ἡeaρτulinʒ,bafl etiam Teut. Vinculum: batten, tenere. Kilian.
units.tr: Hasta, Captivity. Among the Ubii today, likewise prison. Perhaps hasta should be corrected. Saxon captivity is ἁαρτynʒe, and captive ἁαρτulinʒ; also the Teutonic bafl, a bond; batten, to hold. Kilian. [illegible]

units.la: ἱarᴅo, Valde, Nimis] Nobis, eodem senfu, bard, & barolp: valde enim laborare, to labour bard, dicimus: ferió & agrè contendere, sive decertare, nobis barolp to strive or contend. Eopfe senfu, Belg. berε, bard; Germ. bart.
units.tr: Hardo, Very, too much. For us, in the same sense, "bard" and "barolp": for we say "to labour bard", that is, to work very hard; to strive or contend earnestly is for us barolp, "to strive or contend". In the same sense the Dutch have "bere", German "bart".

units.la: ꝑarman, Calumniis] Quod Latin. Læsio, Damnum, nobis barme, à Sax. ἡeaρnmε: per translationem, forte, Calumnia, quod ex eâ fama lædùtur, & damnum datur. Sax. autem calumnia, ἡeaρnmrρρæc.
units.tr: Barman, To calumnies. The Latin is "Læsio", damage or loss; for us barme, from Saxon ἡeaρnmε. Perhaps by transfer, "calumny", because by it one's reputation is hurt and damage is done. Saxon calumnia is ἡeaρnmrρρæc.

units.la: - ꝑategon, Æmulatione] Affonat Sax. ἡaτian, odio habere, quod Teut. baten, & baeten.
units.tr: Pategon, Through emulation. Akin to Saxon ἡatian, to hate, which the Teutonic has as baten and baeten.

units.la: ꝑatongon, Iracundiam] Quicquid fervens (quemadmodum Iracundia) Sax. ἡatɔ, nobis bot.
units.tr: Patongon, Anger. Whatever is fervent (as anger is), Saxon ἡatɔ; for us bot.

units.la: ꝑiegero, Pellicano.
units.tr: Piegero, Pelican.

units.la: ꝑelmoot, & beltmoot. furor] Quod quis, tanquam impos animi, furore actus facit, in the bot mood factum dicimus, uti etiam in the man mood: bot autem, ut suprà in batongon, à Saxon. hæc veniens, ferventem signat; <bl>moode</bl>, Sax. moðe, Teut. <bl>moed</bl>, mentem, animum. Furor autem Sax. hæoheoptnýrre, quasi cordis fervor: animositas, moðmerre.
units.tr: Pelmoot, and beltmoot, Fury. What a man does, as if out of his mind, driven by fury, we call done "in the bot mood", as also "in the man mood". Bot, as above in batongon, comes from the Saxon and signifies fervent; moode, Saxon moðe, Teutonic moed, mind, spirit. Fury in Saxon is hæoheoptnýrre, as if the heat of the heart; animosity is moðmerre.

units.la: Vettinga, Vota. Hodie Galli Soubhaiter, compositè. Vide Gebetta.
units.tr: Vettinga, Vows. Today the French Soubhaiter, in compound form. See Gebetta.

units.la: <bl>Vera</bl>, Cilicio: quasi <bl>baera</bl>, à pilis: & <bl>beren</bl>, cilicium] Cilicium, Saxon. hæna, à pilis, ut Lipsius; nobis <bl>batre-</bl> <bl>ctotb</bl>: Teut. <bl>baere</bl>, & <bl>baerenkleed</bl>, de quo apud Kilian.
units.tr: Vera, Hair shirt: as if baera, from the hairs; and beren, a hair shirt. Hair shirt: Saxon hæna, from the hairs, as Lipsius says; for us "hair-cloth". Teutonic baere, and baerenkleed, on which see Kilian.

units.la: <bl>Vereberga</bl>, Castra. Nos latiùs pro omni diversorio: sed illud proprie & primò: <bl>herbergo</bl>, castrorum] Quatenus universè Diversorium significat, vocem paululùm immutatam habemus: nobis enim, eodem sensu, <bl>bar-</bl> <bl>bour</bl>, de quo in Glossar. Spelman. noster, in voce <bl>herbergare</bl>.
units.tr: Vereberga, Camp. We use it more widely for any lodging; but the proper and first sense is for camps. Insofar as it generally signifies lodging, we have a slightly altered word, which in the same sense is "harbour", on which see our Spelman under the word herbergare.

units.la: <bl>Vevode</bl>, Possessio: supra <bl>Getwin</bl>] Habere, Sax. hæbban, unde, ni fallor, vox ista <bl>bevode</bl>, possessio: sic dicta ab habendo; hinc inops Sax. hæfen leaf.
units.tr: Vevode, Possession: see above Getwin. To have is Saxon hæbban, whence, unless I am mistaken, the word bevode, possession, is so called from having. Hence "destitute" is Saxon hæfen leaf.

units.la: <bl>Vero</bl>, Lutum: vide <bl>bora</bl>.
units.tr: Vero, Mud: see bora.

units.la: <bl>Viera</bl>, Hic] Sax. hea; nobis <bl>here</bl>.
units.tr: Viera, Here. Saxon hea; for us "here".

units.la: Ϸunðeflīga, Cynoma] Hoc Saxon. þunðerþleoȝ, alias þunðlic þleoȝ, id est, mufca canina; ab þunð, nobis ƀound, canis (proprie venaticus, à Sax. þuntan, nobis to ƀunt, venari) & þleoȝ, nobis flþ, mufca.
units.tr: Dunðeflīga, Cynoma. This is Saxon þunðerþleoȝ, otherwise þunðlic þleoȝ, that is, dog-fly; from þunð, for us "hound", dog (properly a hunting dog, from Saxon þuntan, for us "to hunt", to chase), and þleoȝ, for us "fly", a fly.

units.la: Ϸalpilos, Inops: quafi ƀulpeloos] Hoc nobis ƀelpleffe, voce conflata ex ƀelpe, & Sax. & nobis, auxilium, adjutorium; & leffe, quod idem valet in verborum compositione, ac Belg. loos, Ger. lofs, vacuum, deftitutum fignans, de quo plura apud Kilian. in loos. Inops autem Sax. etiam þapenleaȝ, quasi non (five nihil) habens.
units.tr: Halpilos, Needy, as if hulpeloos. For us this is "helpless", compounded from "help", which in Saxon and for us means help or aid, and "less", which in compounds has the same force as the Dutch loos or German los, signifying empty, destitute; more on this in Kilian under loos. Needy, however, in Saxon is also þapenleaȝ, as if not having (or having nothing).

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: Ϸagere, Fœnerator.
units.tr: Ϸagere, Moneylender.

units.la: Ϸbetoanda, Sufpicatus] Nonne hic ineft Sax. penan, opinari, exiftimare? unde noftrum to ƀeene, eodem fenfu.
units.tr: Ϸbetoanda, Suspected] Is not the Saxon penan here, to suppose or to think? Whence our "to ween", in the same sense.

units.la: Ϸemer, Æternum.
units.tr: Ϸemer, Eternal.

units.la: Ϸetoefcon, Æternus. Vide Ϲtolfcon.
units.tr: Ϸetoefcon, Eternal. See Ϲtolfcon.

units.la: Ϸo, Semper] Non multum abludit noftratium Ϸp, eo fenfu.
units.tr: Ϸo, Always] Our own Ϸp does not differ much from it in that sense.

units.la: Ϸo bin, Sum] Sax. ic eom, quibus bin,ut & nobis, verbum præteriti temporis.
units.tr: Ϸo bin, I am] Saxon ic eom; with which "bin", as also for us, is a verb of the past tense.

units.la: Iob, Nonne, Nunquid?
units.tr: Iob, Surely not? Can it be?

units.la: Innethzon, Viscera, Sax. innope, nobis intward.
units.tr: Innethzon, Bowels. Saxon innope; for us, "inward".

units.la: Innerontbingon, Inferioribus] Forte Interioribus, Sax. inpan(alias innepan) Bingum, nobis hodie inner things. Inferior autem Sax. nÿþep, nobis hodie nether, & neder: similiter Teutonicis, dialecto paululum variatâ.
units.tr: Innerontbingon, Inferiors] Perhaps "Interioribus", of inner things. Saxon inpan (otherwise innepan) bingum; for us today "inner things". But "inferior" in Saxon is nÿþep; for us today "nether" and "neder"; similarly in German, with the dialect slightly varied.

units.la: Verba.
units.tr: Verbs.

units.la: Inflouc, Aperuit: vide Anlucon.
units.tr: Inflouc, He opened. See Anlucon.

units.la: Irbelgedon, Exacerbarunt: vide Farbelgeda.
units.tr: Irbelgedon, They provoked. See Farbelgeda.

units.la: Irfangan fal, Increpabit: & irfengge, increpasti.
units.tr: Irfangan fal, He will rebuke; and irfengge, you rebuked.

units.la: Irterron fal, Obstupefacies.
units.tr: Irterron fal, You will astonish.

units.la: Irqnitke, Excita. Irqnitken sal tu, Vivificabis] Vide Gegnitco.
units.tr: Irqnitke, Stir up. Irqnitken sal tu, You will quicken. See Gegnitco.

units.la: Irfcal, Increpuit] Ira, Sax. ÿppe; Irasci, ÿpriian?
units.tr: Irfcal, He rebuked] Anger: Saxon ÿppe; to be angry: ÿpriian?

units.la: Irruozt werthe, Commovear.
units.tr: Irruozt werthe, May I be moved.

units.la: L
units.tr: L

units.la: Lap, Oram veftis] Hoc nobis hodie lap, à Sax. læp, sic dictum forte à Lat. Labium ; quasi vestis labium.
units.tr: Lap, Hem of a garment] This is for us today "lap", from Saxon læp; so perhaps it is called from Latin labium, as if "the lip of a garment".

units.la: <bl>Leqersteoe</bl>, Cubilibus: vide <bl>Ge-</bl> <bl>berge</bl>] Vox est pura puta Saxonica, sed vix, hac notione, eis usurpata, cùm proprie apud eos, (posteriores saltem Saxones) ut lictune, pro Cœmeterio accepta fuerit: composita interim ab eorum liʒʒan.jacere, & s-tzeoe,locus, quasi jacendi locus, ideóque satis accommodè ad cubilia extensa, cùm recubandi loca sint; quæ Monachis Dormitoria dicta, Anglicè <bl>Doɀtoɀs</bl>.
units.tr: Leqersteoe, Couches. See Geberge] This is a pure Saxon word, as it seems, but hardly used by them in this sense, since among them (at least the later Saxons) it was properly taken as lictune, for a cemetery. It is compounded, meanwhile, from their liʒʒan, to lie, and s-tzeoe, place, as if a place for lying; and so quite suitably for extended couches, since they are places for reclining. Monks call these dormitories; in English, "dorters".

units.la: <bl>Lepera</bl>, Labia: hodie <bl>lippen</bl>] Nobis hodie,cum Belg.<bl>lippe</bl>, à Latin. Labium, ni fallor, voce ducta: Sax. enim Labia pælepar.
units.tr: Lepera, Lips. Today "lippen"] For us today, with the Dutch "lippe", derived, unless I am mistaken, from Latin labium; for the Saxon word for lips is pælepar.

units.la: <bl>Letistou</bl>, Novissima : nunc <bl>letten</bl>] Hinc,forte,ultimus,nobis <bl>last</bl>,& <bl>latest</bl>.
units.tr: Letistou, the newest; now letten. Hence, perhaps, our "last" and "latest," from the same root as the Latin ultimus.

units.la: <bl>Lıbe</bl>, Vita : & <bl>libes</bl>, vitæ : & <bl>lif</bl>,vitam. Nos <bl>leve</bl>: tamen & vulgò, <bl>lobe</bl>,illo sensu] Vita,Sax.lip,unde nostrum <bl>life</bl>, quod Belg. <bl>lpf</bl>, <bl>lief</bl>, Teut. <bl>leben</bl>.
units.tr: Lıbe, life; libes, of life; and lif, life. We have "leve," though it is also commonly "lobe" in that sense. Life: Saxon lip, whence our "life," which the Dutch write lpf or lief and the Teutons leben.

units.la: <bl>Lifware</bl>, Cibaria : quasi <bl>lpf-waere</bl>] Porcelli, & cætera animalia tenella à Rusticis domi nutrita hinc (forte) nobis dicta <bl>lpware</bl>. Cibus etiam nobis <bl>fare</bl>; Sax. bizleopa.
units.tr: Lifware, Victuals, as if "life-ware"] Piglets and other tender animals reared at home by country folk; hence perhaps we call them "lpware". Food is also "fare" for us; Saxon bizleopa.

units.la: <bl>Lockis</bl>,
units.tr: Lockis,

units.la: Lockis, Capilli: & lockis, capillis] Hæc nobis cum Germanis & superioribus & inferioribus. lockis:eodem sensu Sax. loccar?
units.tr: Lockis, Hair; and lockis, of hair] These are for us, as for the Germans, both upper and lower. Lockis: in the same sense, Saxon loccar?

units.la: Lofen, Dolofum: & lofin, dolofo: & lofonga, dolos] His affine Saxon. læpunʒe, unde nostrum leasing, mendacium.
units.tr: Lofen, of deceit; and lofin, by deceit; and lofonga, deceits] Akin to these is Saxon læpunʒe, whence our "leasing", a lie.

units.la: Los, Sortem] Hoc nobis cum Belg. lot à Sax. ɧlot, & ɧlỳt, fors. Æpenɧlỳtta, consors.
units.tr: Los, Lot] This is for us, as for the Dutch "lot", from Saxon ɧlot and ɧlỳt, chance. Æpenɧlỳtta, a partner.

units.la: Lucucumin, Paulominus: nos lut-telkemin.
units.tr: Lucucumin, A little less: for us lut-telkemin.

units.la: Luctika, Pusilla.
units.tr: Luctika, Little (feminine).

units.la: Luzzilon, Parvulis: & luticon, idem] Parvuli Sax. lɪttlinʒar, nobis little ones, quod Germ. superiores, ȝ. pro f. amantes, habent Luzzilon.
units.tr: Luzzilon, little ones; and luticon, the same. The Saxon lɪttlinʒar is our "little ones." The upper Germans, who write ȝ for f and love such forms, have Luzzilon.

units.la: Luogindo, Rugiens: & luonde, rugientes, alibi] Ejusdem originis, ac nostrum lotw, aliàs bellotw. Vox fictitia, à sono bovis mugientis, cujus mugitus, Sax. ʒeɧlop. Mugire autem Belg. loten, Ger. lupen.
units.tr: Luogindo, Roaring; and luonde, roaring (plural), elsewhere] Of the same origin as our "lowe", or elsewhere "bellow". It is a made-up word, from the sound of a lowing ox, whose lowing in Saxon is ʒeɧlop. To low is Dutch loten, German lupen.

units.la: Verba.
units.tr: Verbs.

units.la: Liconf, Placent: vide Gelliconda: & liconsal, Placebit] Pro geliconda hîc, repone gelicoda, quod vide.
units.tr: Liconf, They please. See Gelliconda; and liconsal, he will please] Here, for gelliconda, read gelicoda, which see.

units.la: Ludon,
units.tr: Ludon,

units.la: Ʒ Ludon fal,Tonabit: nos de æ re Campano] Sonorus nobis loud, Sax.Ꝑluoe, Belg.lupd, Teut. laut.
units.tr: Ʒ Ludon fal, He will thunder] We, on the same matter, (see Campanus). Sonorous: for us "loud"; Saxon Ꝑluoe, Dutch lupd, German laut.

units.la: Ʒ Lutwetha, Præstitisti.
units.tr: Ʒ Lutwetha, You performed.

units.la: M
units.tr: M

units.la: Spancrefte,Majestas: ipsa vox tamen viri robur magis significat, manscracht. sed alibi, megtncraft, majestas: & megtncrefti, majestatis] Hoc Sax.mæzenSþymnej, & mæzenþpimmej, quasi magnum firmamentum; à mæzen, magnum, & Sþymnej, alias tpumnej, firmamentum, à getpymman, stabilire: & proprie, utpote de Deo dictum.
units.tr: Spancrefte, Majesty] Yet the word itself rather signifies a man's strength, manscracht. But elsewhere megtncraft, majesty; and megtncrefti, of majesty] This is Saxon mæzenSþymnej and mæzenþpimmej, as if "great firmament"; from mæzen, great, and Sþymnej, otherwise tpumnej, firmament, from getpymman, to establish. It is properly said, as being said of God.

units.la: Spangon, Maxillas: si recta scriptura: nos wangen] Similiter & Saxones, uti & nos, saltem olim. Majoribus enim nostris maxilla, sive dentes maxillares, wang·teeth dicti, à wang, gena, maxilla: unde rythmus ille vetus: And in witnesse that this is sooth; I bite the war with my wang tooth: id est, In testimonium veritatis, hanc ceram mordeo dente meo maxillari. De quo fusius alibi, in Glossar. nostro.
units.tr: Spangon, jaws (if the reading is correct): we say "wangen." The Saxons did the same, as we also did, at least in former times. For our ancestors, the jaw or the jaw teeth were called "wang-teeth," from wang, meaning cheek or jaw. Hence that old rhyme: And in witnesse that this is sooth; I bite the war with my wang tooth, that is, In testimony of the truth, I bite this wax with my jaw tooth. I discuss this more fully elsewhere, in our Glossary.

units.la: Spelm Pulvis: nos malm,& gemul] Hoc Sax.myl.
units.tr: Spelm, Dust] For us "malm" and "gemul". This is Saxon myl.

units.la: Speltero,
units.tr: Speltero,

units.la: Weltero, Maximo : nos meest] Nos Angli most : Sax. mærta ?
units.tr: Weltero, Greatest] We English say most. Saxon mærta?

units.la: Wendlse, Lætitia : vide Wendlan.
units.tr: Wendlse, Joy. See Wendlan.

units.la: Wiedon,Mercis] Merces Sax.meoe, nobis meed. Eis etiam Munera(bzlbes) meaorceaττaɾ ?
units.tr: Wiedon, reward. Saxon meoe, for us "meed," is the word for wages or reward. For them also gifts (bzlbes) [meoaorceaττaɾ?]

units.la: Wiuel, Magnus, Multa, Copiosa : & mikilon,magnis : & mikilo magnificè : & oimikilt, magnificate. vide Wimfkiloda : & mikle,magnificentia] Multús Saxon.mycel, hactenus in partibus Angliæ Borealibus retentum. Multitudo, mycelnerre; magnificare autem, zemiclian; magnificentia, myclunz, & mycelnyr ?
units.tr: Wiuel, Great, Many, Abundant; and mikilon, to great ones; and mikilo, magnificently; and oimikilt, magnified. See Wimfkiloda; and mikle, magnificence] Saxon mycel, "much", retained so far in the Northern parts of England. Multitude, mycelnerre; but to magnify, zemiclian; magnificence, myclunz, and mycelnyr?

units.la: Wuodis, Mentis : nos, moezt] Vide supra Wefmodl.
units.tr: Wuodis, Of mind. For us "moez t". See above Wefmodl.

units.la: Wuos, Esca, cibi. Nos pro Olere] Huic,sono saltem,affine; Sax. myre,& mere,pro Mensa : iis etiam mete pro cibo : nobis hodie mette pro ferculo.
units.tr: Wuos, Food, of food. For us, for Olere (herbs)] Akin to this, at least in sound: Saxon myre and mere, for table; for them also mete for food; for us today mette, for a dish.

units.la: Wulca, Passer.
units.tr: Wulca, Sparrow.

units.la: Verba.
units.tr: Words.

units.la: Wendlan sal, Exsultabo : mendita, exsultabit : mendit, exsultate : mendodun, exsultaverunt : mendon salon, exsultabunt.
units.tr: Wendlan sal, I shall exult: mendita, he shall exult: mendit, exult ye: mendodun, they have exulted: mendon salon, they shall exult.

units.la: N
units.tr: N

units.la: <bl>Bado</bl>, sed: & <bl>Bajo</bl>, paenè] Pænè, nobis nigb, & well-nigb: g. in utrâq; voce superfluo, vel otioso, & inter pronuntiandum neglecto, quin & inter scribendum perperam usurpato: à Sax. enim vocem accepimus, quibus, nih & ful-nieh scripta.
units.tr: <bl>Bado</bl>, but: & <bl>Bajo</bl>, almost] Pæne, to us nigh, and well-nigh. The g is superfluous in each word, idle, neglected in pronunciation, and even wrongly used in writing. For we took the word from the Saxon, in which it is written nih and ful-nieh.

units.la: <bl>Beock</bl>, Nec] Sax.nic ?
units.tr: <bl>Beock</bl>, Nor] Saxon nic?

units.la: <bl>Berlando</bl>, salutare: & <bl>Berlando</bl>, liberator] Refugium, Sax.zeneh, quod ab eorum zenehian fluens, eruere, eripere, signat: hinc Dominus & Redemptor noster, nenzeno urrep Sax. dictus.
units.tr: <bl>Berlando</bl>, to save: & <bl>Berlando</bl>, deliverer] Refuge, Saxon zeneh, which, flowing from their zenehian, signifies to rescue or snatch away. Hence our Lord and Redeemer is called in Saxon nenzeno urrep.

units.la: Benwthf, Nequam: quasi dicas, nullius pretii aut ponderis] Nequitia, uti & Malitia, Sax.nyhe, & nihe: Man etiam illo sensu usurparunt: unde Nequam, Malus, eis manpulle: ; ab homini naturali nequitiâ. A nihe autem, Nequam vocárunt nihinz; Unde illud apud Mat.Parif. & alios: Rex (inquit) milites Anglos, ut ad obsidionem veniant, jubet.: nisi velint sub nomine NITHING, quod Latinè Nequam sonat, recenseri, &c. Vocabulum hoc, Nithing, thing, þing, à nocte venire conjecit Glossographus ibidem; quæ (inquit) olim Þitþ, non ut nunc (nigþt) scripta reperitur: Ita ut Þithing sit Lucifuga, &c. Fugit interim doctum virum vera vocis scriptura. Nox enim perperam apud Anglos scribitur, sive Þitþ sive Þigþt; rectè autem, & secundum Sax. scribendi modum, niht. Utut sit, luce clarius est, nihthing, cum Nequam notet, à Sax: niþe, nequitia, malitia, dimanasse.
units.tr: <bl>Benwthf</bl>, Worthless: as if you said, of no worth or weight] Wickedness, like Malice, is Saxon nyhe and nihe. They also used it in that sense, whence Nequam, wicked, is eis manpulle, from natural human wickedness. From nihe they called the worthless nihinz. Hence that passage in Matthew Paris and others: "The king (he says) orders the English soldiers to come to the siege, unless they wish to be enrolled under the name NITHING, which in Latin means Nequam, etc." The gloss-writer there conjectured that this word, <bl>Nithing</bl>, comes from night (nocte). He says that what was formerly written <bl>Þitþ</bl>, not as now (<bl>nigþt</bl>), so that <bl>Þithing</bl> means one who flees the light, etc. Yet the learned man misses the true spelling of the word. For night is wrongly written among the English, whether as <bl>Þitþ</bl> or <bl>Þigþt</bl>; correctly, and according to the Saxon manner of writing, it is <bl>niht</bl>. However that may be, it is clearer than light that <bl>nihthing</bl>, since it signifies Nequam, has flowed from the Saxon <bl>niþe</bl>, wickedness, malice.

units.la: <bl>Þewþ</bl>, Pravum] Quemadmodum hoc præcedenti, sic & huic affine nostrum <bl>naught</bl>, & <bl>naughtp</bl>, illo sensu, à <bl>niþe</bl> ortum.
units.tr: <bl>Þewþ</bl>, Perverse] As with the preceding, so our cognate <bl>naught</bl> and <bl>naughty</bl> in that sense arose from <bl>niþe</bl>.

units.la: <bl>Þithiebt</bl>, Non; & <bl>nauhiebt</bl>, idem.
units.tr: <bl>Þithiebt</bl>, Not; and <bl>nauhiebt</bl>, the same.

units.la: <bl>Þiewergen</bl>, & <bl>ntergin</bl>, Usquequaque.
units.tr: <bl>Þiewergen</bl>, and <bl>ntergin</bl>, Everywhere.

units.la: <bl>Þorthalbon</bl>, Aquilonis] A <bl>Þorth</bl>, & <bl>halfe</bl>, eâpse apud Sax. significatione.
units.tr: <bl>Þorthalbon</bl>, of the North] From <bl>Þorth</bl> and <bl>halfe</bl>, with the same meaning in Saxon.

units.la: <bl>Þoban</bl>, Sed: suprà <bl>Þabo</bl>.
units.tr: <bl>Þoban</bl>, But: see above <bl>Þabo</bl>.

units.la: <bl>Þobanthog</bl>, Veruntamen] A superiori <bl>noban</bl>, & <bl>thog</bl>, Sax: <bl>Þeah</bl>, nobis <bl>though</bl>, tamen.
units.tr: Þobanthog, Veruntamen] From the preceding noban, and thog, Saxon Þeah, which we now write though, meaning "however" (tamen).

units.la: Verba:
units.tr: Words:

units.la: <bl>Þerufsaf</bl>, & <bl>Þeruohlf</bl>, Nolite: & <bl>Þeruoht</bl>, Noli. Plet, Posside: & Pletson sal, Possidebit: & Patun, Possidere] Omnia à Sax. notian, uti, possidere, occupare.
units.tr: <bl>Þerufsaf</bl>, and <bl>Þeruohlf</bl>, Do not ye: and <bl>Þeruoht</bl>, Do not thou. Plet, Possess: and Pletson sal, He shall possess: and Patun, To possess] All from Saxon notian, to use, possess, occupy.

units.la: Mosada, Impedivit.
units.tr: Mosada, Hindered.

units.la: G.
units.tr: G.

units.la: Dveranungtscobt, Supervacuè] Ab ober, Teuton. Sax. Anglis, super; un, particulâ negativâ, sive privativâ; & gefcobt, proventus: ungtscobt itaque q. d. sine fructu, frustrà, Sax. opepunnyt.
units.tr: Dveranungtscobt, In vain] From <bl>ober</bl>, Teutonic, Saxon, English over, super; un, a negative or privative particle; and <bl>gefcobt</bl>, profit. So <bl>ungtscobt</bl> means, as if to say, without fruit, in vain; Saxon opepunnyt.

units.la: DvirbozIga, Prævaricantes: vel potius Mandatum spernentes] Conjectura placet; cum inde fit, quod contemptus, despectio, contumacia, Saxonib. opepbynnerre dicta. Mulcta etiam, quâ talis contemptus luebatur, comprehendit, quæ Forensibus nostris Forisfactura dicta.
units.tr: DvirbozIga, Transgressing: or rather, despising the command] This conjecture pleases, since from it comes contempt, disdain, and obstinacy, called in Saxon opepbynnerre. It also covers the fine by which such contempt was atoned for, which our lawyers call Forisfactura.

units.la: Dvita, Pomoruum. Nos Doff] Sax. opaet, aliàs opet. eodem sensu, scil. pro frugibus, &c.
units.tr: Dvita, Crops. We Doff] Saxon opaet, otherwise opet, in the same sense, namely for crops, etc.

units.la: Verba.
units.tr: Words.

units.la: Digt, Ostende, ab oculis ductum. Dgtnon, Ostendet: & Dugoda, idem: & Dugon sal, Ostendam] Ab oculis recte conjicit; Sax.enim Oculus eaze: nobis, z. in y mutato, Ep. Saxonico autem propius Teut. Aug. uti & Belg. Degbe.
units.tr: Digt, Show, derived from eyes. Dgtnon, He will show: and Dugoda, the same: and Dugon sal, I will show] He rightly conjectures from eyes. For the Saxon for eye is eaze, with z changed for y; but closer to the Saxon is Teutonic Aug., and also Belgic Degbe.

units.la: Dioon, Habitabat. Hoida Tartarorum] Habitare Sax. eapoian, & oneapoian. Habitatio hinc eis eapounzrtop; rtop autem locus: alteram compositi partem mitto, ut omnibus, ex praemissis, satis obviam.
units.tr: Dioon, Dwelt. Hoida of the Tartars] Saxon eapoian, and oneapoian, to dwell. Hence dwelling is eis eapounzrtop, and rtop means place. I leave out the other part of the compound, since from what has been said it is sufficiently clear to everyone.

units.la: P Pisina, Usura. Q
units.tr: P Pisina, Usury. Q

units.la: Queena, Uxor. Anglis hodie Regis uxor ἐξόχως, five Regina] Distinguimus Angli inter Queen, & Queen; posteriore, scortum, meretricem; priore, Reginam, Regis uxorem, intelligentes. Ortu vero & Origine vox una & eadem, Quen scil. quod uxorem, sive mulierem signat; ut ealocpene, Aniculam. Quamvis enim consuetudine, Queane, in malam partem transierit apud neotericos, olim tamen secus, nisi Hoi praepositio, quasi uxor vel mulier pretio conducta: qua de re vide plura supra, in Debuoiua.
units.tr: Queena, Wife. Among the English today, the king's wife, preeminently, or Queen] We English distinguish between Queen and Queen: the latter means a harlot or whore, the former the Queen, the king's wife. In origin and derivation the word is one and the same, Quen, which signifies wife or woman, as in ealocpene, an old woman. For although by custom Queane has passed into a bad sense among modern writers, formerly it was otherwise, unless the preposition Hoi is added, as if a wife or woman hired for a price. On this matter see more above, under Debuoiua.

units.la: Hh3 Quic-
units.tr: Hh3 Quic-

units.la: Quiccafe, Animalia: quasi Quictee, vivæ pecudes] Vide supra, Qe- quicco, & Ffo.
units.tr: Quiccafe, Animals: as if Quictee, living beasts] See above, Qequicco, and Ffo.

units.la: Verba.
units.tr: Words.

units.la: Quat, Dixit: & Quethe, Dicat: & Qulf, Dic. Nobis manfit geminatione vitiofum, Quetteren] Sax. cpeban, dicere, unde noftrum quoth, ut quoth 3, dixi ego: quoth be, dixit ille, & fimil. Vide plura apud Kilian. Etymolog. verbo quetteren.
units.tr: Quat, Said: and Quethe, Let him say: and Qulf, Say. Our manfit, faulty by doubling, Quetteren] Saxon cpeban, to say, whence our quoth: quoth I, I said; quoth he, he said; and similar. See more in Kilian's Etymologicum under quetteren.

units.la: Quezzedos, Allififti. Nos quetfen.
units.tr: Quezzedos, Thou hast accused. We quetfen.

units.la: R
units.tr: R

units.la: Ratannth, Irritatione. vide Rafa- don.
units.tr: Ratannth, Irritation. See Rafadon.

units.la: Radiwagen, Currus: quasi Radtwagen, à celeritate: an & Rtedwaegen, ab ufu? Iftinc Reda] Ejufmodi vehiculum, à currendo, Currum, Latini; pyne, Sax. vocabant. Hic autem Radiwagen dicitur, eadem de caufa ac noftrum Rode-wagen, à via publicà fcil. (ubi præcipuus curruum ufus) nobis Rode dicta, majoribus noftris Rade, à Saxon. pade, equitatio: via publica fic dicta, quia equitationibus, & & equis iter facientibus veluti propria.
units.tr: Radiwagen, Chariot: as if Radtwagen, from speed; or Rtedwaegen, from use? Hence Reda. The Latins called this kind of vehicle, from running, currum; the Saxons called it pyne. Here it is called Radiwagen for the same reason as our Rode-wagen, from the public road, namely the one where carriages are chiefly used. We call it Rode; our ancestors called it Rade, from Saxon pade, riding. A public road is so called because it belongs, as it were, to riders and to those travelling on horses.

units.la: Ref, Venter: & Rebis, Ventris : & Rebe, Ventre] Alvus & Uterus Sax. Pnÿpe,alias Pnip.Hinc Diaphragma, quod dividit & sepatat ventrem & interstina à pulmone & corde,nobis mtō-rtffe, Belgis mtoDelrpffe.
units.tr: Ref, Belly: and Rebis, of the belly: and Rebe, in the belly] Alvus and uterus are Saxon Pnÿpe, otherwise Pnip. Hence the diaphragm, which divides and separates the belly and intestines from the lungs and heart, is to us mtō-rtffe, to the Belgians mtoDelrpffe.

units.la: <bl>Rtpoton</bl>, Maturitate : nobis <bl>Rtjp</bl> manfit] Anglis etiam, maturus, <bl>rtpe</bl> : maturitas, <bl>rtpeneffe</bl> ; Saxon. pipunza. Meffis autem eis pip : metere, pipan : meffor pipepe, alias pipepe : falx, pipepen; unde nobis <bl>rtppting,reapting</bl>; pro meffione : <bl>Rtpper</bl>, <bl>Reaper</bl>, pro meffore, & fimil.
units.tr: <bl>Rtpoton</bl>, Ripeness: our <bl>Rtjp</bl> remained] Among the English also, ripe is <bl>rtpe</bl>; ripeness <bl>rtpeneffe</bl>; Saxon pipunza. Harvest is pip, to reap is pipan, a reaper is pipepe (otherwise pipepe), a sickle is pipepen; whence our reaping, for harvesting, and Reaper, for reaper, and similar.

units.la: <bl>Rttba</bl>, Tofrens] Hoc Saxon. pip, Cambro-Britannis, Vadum <bl>Rbpb</bl>, & <bl>Rbpble</bl>. Vox autem reperitur in nonnullarum urbium,ut & oppidorum noftrorum,Gallicorumque nominibus ad vada conftructorum, ut apud Chorographum noftrum, praesentiff. Cambd. videre licet.
units.tr: <bl>Rttba</bl>, Torrent] This is Saxon pip. To the Cambro-Britons a ford is <bl>Rbpb</bl> and <bl>Rbpble</bl>. The word is found in the names of some cities and of our towns, and of Gallic places built at fords, as may be seen in our chorographer Camden, presently.

units.la: Verba.
units.tr: Words.

units.la: <bl>Ratodon</bl>, Irritaverunt : & <bl>Ratuof</bl>, Irritat : & <bl>Deratot</bl> (t), Concitatus est: & <bl>Ratunuffi</bl>, Irritatione] Huic affine noftrum <bl>wzatb</bl>, iram, iracundiam,
units.tr: Ratodon, They have provoked; Ratuof, He provokes; Deratot (t), He is provoked; Ratunuffi, Provocation. Akin to this is our wrath, signifying anger, ire.

units.la: signans. Ssnstt, autem hic, ut & in pluribus aliis vocibus, tum præcedentibus, tum subsequentibus, adjectitia est particula, idem valens ac apud nos & Sax. nefle, & npsse, Teut. best; & hepo, in nominum substantivorum terminatione.
units.tr: Here Ssnstt, as in many other words both preceding and following, is an added particle, having the same force as among us and in Saxon "nefle" and "npsse," and in Teutonic "best," and "hepo" in the ending of substantive nouns.

units.la: Ʀtbarɪdoȹ, Denudasti: sic nobis compositum, Openbaeren. Rebarnust, Revelatione] Nudus, nobis Anglis, bare ; denudare, to make bare.
units.tr: Ʀtbarɪdoȹ, You have uncovered; so compounded among us, "Openbaeren" (to reveal). Rebarnust, Revelation. Nudus, among us English "bare"; denudare, "to make bare."

units.la: Refangan, Arguam, & Refagnust, Redargutiones.
units.tr: Refangan, I shall argue; Refagnust, refutations.

units.la: Refplas, Arguas. Nos componimus Werlspen.
units.tr: Refplas, you argue. We compound it as "Werlspen."

units.la: Ʀuecont, Fumigabant: quia Roof, Fumus: sed & alio sensu, Rtecbon sun, Fumigabunt, ab odore] Fumus, Sax. pec; fumare, peocan, unde nostrum reeke, fumus: item to reeke, Belg. Rooken, fumare. Ifthinc etiam (forte) nubium ex vento motum, nos racke dicimus.
units.tr: Ʀuecont, They were fumigating, because Roof means smoke; but also in another sense, Rtecbon sun, they will fumigate, from the odour. Smoke, Saxon "pec"; to smoke, "peocan," whence our "reeke," smoke; likewise "to reeke," Dutch "Rooken," to fume. If from this also (perhaps) we call the motion of clouds by the wind "racke."

units.la: Roowarthan, Movebitur] Hinc forte Cœlum noœpe Sax. dictum, à movendo scil. quia semper movet: Warthan nihil aliud hic nisi verbi passivi futuri temporis nota.
units.tr: Roowarthan, It will be moved. Hence perhaps the heaven was called by the Saxons (from moving, namely because it always moves). "Warthan" here is nothing other than the mark of the passive future tense.

units.la: Rundon, Sufurrabunt] Sufurrare, muffitare, Sax. punian: Belg. Runen, Roener, nobis hodie to rounde, & rounde, de quo plura per Spelman.noftr. in Wormii Literatura Runica, cap. 1.
units.tr: Rundon, They will murmur. To murmur, mutter: Saxon "punian"; Dutch "Runen," "Roener"; among us today "to rounde" and "rounde," about which more may be found in Spelman, our countryman, in Wormius's Literatura Runica, chap. 1.

units.la: S.
units.tr: S.

units.la: <bl>Saca</bl>, Rem] Sax. Caufa, rac & race: unde noftrum fake, ut Dei intuitu, vulgo dicimus, fo; <bl>Gods</bl> fake. Proprie tamen Res, Saxon. <bl>Zinz</bl>, quod nobis manfit.
units.tr: Saca, Thing. Saxon "caufa," "rac" and "race"; whence our "fake," as we commonly say "for God's fake." Properly, however, Res is Saxon "Zinz," which has remained with us.

units.la: <bl>Salda</bl>, Salutare: & <bl>Saldo</bl>.
units.tr: Salda, to save; and Saldo.

units.la: Saletbu, Tabernaculo: & Selt- thon, Tabernacula, & Seltha, Tabernaculum. Nos falett, paulo alio sensu] Hoc Sax. zerele. Belgis fale, pro Aula, Atrium: olim autem pro universa domo sumptum fuit; De quo in De variis Glossematis, Cl. Vossius, in voce Sala.
units.tr: Saletbu, to a tabernacle; and Selthon, tabernacles; and Seltha, a tabernacle. We have "falett" in a slightly different sense. This is Saxon "zerele." To the Dutch "fale" means hall or atrium; but formerly it was taken for the whole house. Concerning this, in De variis Glossematis, the learned Vossius, under the word Sala.

units.la: <bl>Sammung</bl>, Synagoga. Unde <bl>Verfae-</bl> <bl>men</bl>, & <bl>fammongun</bl>, Cleros, causa collectionis] Synagoga Sax. <bl>zeromnun-</bl> <bl>za</bl>, ab eorum <bl>zeromnian</bl> fluens, quod congregare notat.
units.tr: Sammung, synagogue; whence "Verfaemen" and "fammongun," lot, cause of gathering. The Saxon for synagogue is "zeromnunza," flowing from their "zeromnian," which means to gather.

units.la: Scale, Servus. Unde Maris-scalcus, qui equis curator] Servus Sax. zcealc;
units.tr: Scale, servant; whence Marisscalcus, one who tends horses. Saxon "zcealc" for servant.

units.la: Hac autem de voce, Cl. Lindenbrog. & Voff. in Scalcus, & Adelfcalc, aliique.
units.tr: On this word see the learned Lindenbrog and Vossius, under Scalcus and Adelfcalc, and others.

units.la: <bl>Scaebon</bl>, Pudore] Vide <bl>Gefcen- bedi.</bl>
units.tr: Scaebon, shame. See "Gefcenbedi."

units.la: <bl>Scaphon</bl>, Ovili] Hoc Sax. rceapafalo, unde.noftrum fheepfolo: voce effidâ à rceap, nobis fheep, & falo, nobis folo, Septum, Clauftrum, quo ex cratibus facto, paftores nocte includunt oves, tum ad ftercorandum arva, tum ne in fegetes fpatientur.
units.tr: Scaphon, sheepfold. This is Saxon "rceapafalo," whence our "sheepfold": a word compounded of "rceap" (our "sheep") and "falo" (our "fold"), an enclosure made of hurdles, in which shepherds shut the sheep at night, both to manure the fields and so that they do not stray into the crops.

units.la: <bl>Scama</bl>,Reverentia] Hoc Saxonibus rceame,rcame; & rcamu, à rceamian & rcamian, id eft,& erubefcere, & revereri. Iftinc autem noftrum <bl>fhame</bl>; eopfe fenfu;quod Belg.<bl>fchaemte</bl>,Teut. <bl>fcham.</bl>
