units.tr: Scama, reverence. For the Saxons "rceame," "rcame," and "rcamu," from "rceamian" and "rcamian," that is, to be ashamed and to revere. Hence our "shame," in the same sense; the Dutch "schaemte," the Teutonic "scham."

units.la: Scarfabs,Novacula.Nam fabs,cultrum notat: unde Saxones Withikindo] Hoc Sax. rcenprax. Vox eft confata ex Saxon. rceapan, Belg. fcheren, & fchaeren, radere, tondere; (unde noftratium fhears, Forfex; fhearing, Tonfura; fherman, Pannitonfor:) & rax,quod praeter novaculam, cultrum fignat. De quo Galfrid. nofter Momemuthen, lib. 4, cap. 3. fufius autem Verstegan. Restitut. cap. 1. & Voss. in voce Saxa.
units.tr: Scarfabs, razor. For "fabs" denotes a knife; whence the Saxons ... Withikindo. This is Saxon "rcenprax." The word is compounded from Saxon "rceapan," Dutch "scheren" and "schaeren," to shave, to shear (whence our "shears," scissors; "shearing," tonsure; "sherman," a cloth-shearer); and "rax," which signifies a knife as well as a razor. On this see our Geoffrey of Monmouth, Momemuthen, book 4, chap. 3; more fully Verstegan, Restitutio, chap. 1, and Vossius under the word Saxa.

units.la: Scefti, vel fcepfti, fagittæ] Hæc Sax. rcefrar, nobis hodie shafts, forte à thave, Teut. schaben, tondere, radere, ut Sagittæ radi solent ab Arcuariis: nisi à sceaf malis, i, e. Fascis: quòd sagittæ in fasces solent colligari, unde nobis a theaf of arrowes.
units.tr: Scefti, or scepfti, arrows. These are Saxon "rcefrar," which we now call "shafts," perhaps from "thave," Teutonic "schaben," to shave or scrape, as arrows are commonly scraped by bowyers; unless from "sceaf" (malis), that is, a bundle, because arrows are commonly bound into bundles, whence among us "a sheaf of arrows."

units.la: Scepeno, Judex: hodie scepenen, scabini] De hoc plura apud sæpius laudat. Lindenbrog. & Voss.
units.tr: Scepeno, judge; today "scepenen," scabini. More about this is found in the frequently cited Lindenbrog and Vossius.

units.la: Sceithlon, Verticem, & scetlon] Scýtehealo Sax, præceps, item oblìquus.
units.tr: Sceithlon, the top of the head; and scetlon. Saxon "Scýtehealo," headlong; likewise sloping.

units.la: Scerns, Subsannatio; & scern, illusio] scorne nobis, eodem sensu.
units.tr: Scerns, derision; and scern, mockery. Among us "scorne," in the same sense.

units.la: Sclert, Lucidum] Limpidus, clarus, nobis sheere, & shire, unde aqua ejusmodi, nobis sheer (vel shire) water. Hinc oppidi & castri apud Dorsetenses nostros, Shirborne dicti, nominis origo: quòd scil. ad Fontem limpidum situm sit. Cambden.
units.tr: Sclert, bright. Limpid, clear; among us "sheere" and "shire," whence such water is called "sheer (or shire) water." Hence the origin of the name of the town and castle called Shirborne among our Dorsetshire people: because, namely, it lies by a limpid spring. Camden.

units.la: Sctimo, Splendor: nos schijne] Angli similiter; voce ortâ à Sax. rciman, splendere, fulgere.
units.tr: Sctimo, splendour. We say "schijne" (shine); the English likewise, the word arising from Saxon "rciman," to shine, gleam.

units.la: Scieumo, Citò] Nobis to fkime, eo-dem dem fenfu : E.G. fo fkime ober anp tbing, id eft,expedite tranfire,vel tranfilire. Vide fuprà ⊙ltfatunDon.
units.tr: Scieumo, quickly. Among us "to skime," in the same sense: e.g. "so skime ober any thing," that is, to pass or leap over something quickly. See above under "Ⓞltfatun Don."

units.la: Belgæ]Non multum abit à noftratium foztotw, quod à Sax. ranz, dolor.
units.tr: The Dutch word is not far from our "sorrow," which comes from Saxon "ranz," grief.

units.la: Hoc nobis feate, & fettle, Sax. rectl : utrumque ab eorum rirtan, federe.
units.tr: We have this as "seat" and "settle," Saxon "rectl"; both from their "rirtan," to settle.

units.la: Hoc Sax. revlzonz, & revellunz, à retl, fedes, & zanzan, ire ; quafi Seffum ire ; unde noftrum fanne go to, eodem fenfu.
units.tr: Saxon "revlzonz" and "revellunz," from "retl," a seat, and "zanzan," to go; as if to go seating. Whence our "fanne go to," in the same sense.

units.la: Huic refpondet noftratium feare woob, pro Cremio, vel Ramale,à Sax. reapan, arefacere, & putu, fylva, lignum, vulgò woob.
units.tr: To this corresponds our "fear wood," meaning faggot or bough, from Saxon "reapan," to dry up, and "putu," forest, wood, commonly "wood."

units.la: Nonne hinc noftrum fkrine, Diathyrum fcil. item Umbella? Saxonibus autem,hoc fenfu, rcpimbpe, fcil.pro Protectore.
units.tr: Hence our "skrine"? Namely Diathyrum; likewise Umbella? For the Saxons, in this sense, "rcpimbpe," that is, a protector.

units.la: Mores Sax. riba?
units.tr: Mores, Saxon "riba"?

units.la: Sitwolbatdun, Septuplum: quasi sevenwoudt] Hoc nobis sevenfold, à Sax. reofonpealo ȝ
units.tr: Sitwolbatdun, Septuplum: as if sevenwoudt. This is our "sevenfold", from the Saxon reofonpealo and

units.la: Sten-ogun, Pupilla oculi] Hoc Sax. reon-eazan, quasi Visus oculi, à reon, Sax. videre, & eaz; oculus, alias æpl; unde nostratium Apple of the Eye.
units.tr: Sten-ogun, the pupil of the eye. This is Saxon "reon-eazan," as if the sight of the eye, from "reon," Saxon to see, and "eaz," eye (elsewhere "æpl"); whence our Apple of the Eye.

units.la: Sigtmart, Victor. in Tacito, Seglmerus] Victoria, Sax. rige: victoriofus, rigæpest: Mart autem hic in Sig-tmart, à mæpe duclum arbitror, quod magnum, celebrem, præstantem sonat.
units.tr: Sigtmart, victor; in Tacitus, Seglmerus. Victory is Saxon "rige," victorious "rigæpest." But I think Mart here in Sig-tmart is derived from "mæpe," which means great, famous, excellent.

units.la: Stu, Utquid?
units.tr: Stu, why?

units.la: Slaptgravt, Sepulcrum: suprà Burgift] Sepulcrum nobis hodie a grave, à Sax. grave; Verstegano slapigrava, q. sleep-grave, quia (inquit) sepultus tanquam dormiens habendus est. Conjecturam probo, cum dormire, nobis sit to sleep, à Sax. slapan. Sepulcrum hinc vocatur Dormitorium.
units.tr: Slaptgravt, sepulchre; above, Burgift. Among us today the sepulchre is "a grave," from Saxon "grave." Verstegan has "slapigrava," that is "sleep-grave," because (he says) the buried man is to be regarded as sleeping. I approve this conjecture, since among us "to sleep" is "to sleep," from Saxon "slapan." Hence the sepulchre is called a dormitory.

units.la: Slabta, Generatio: & slabsen, femini. Nos compositè Geslacht.
units.tr: Slabta, generation; and slabsen, offspring. Among us compounded as "Geslacht."

units.la: Sptetis, Hasta. Nos spleste. Nomen primogenium à mucrone, sptets] Hoc Belg. spet, speet, unde forte nostrum spit, Veru. Hasta autem Sax. rpepe, quod nobis manset.
units.tr: Sptetis, spear. Among us "spleste." Its primary name is from the point (sptets). This is Dutch "spet," "speet," whence perhaps our "spit," a roasting spit. The Saxon for spear is "rpepe," which has remained with us.

units.la: Spinco, Locusta] A saltu (ni fallor) ductum: quia saltu se propellere solet Locusta. Salire autem nobis to springing. Exultavit infans in utero ejus: Luc. 1. ver. 41. id est, (ut vetustiores nostrae Translationes locum reddunt) The Babe springang in her belly. Hinc Saxon. Locusta zæpṗtapa, & zæpṗhopp, à zæpṗ nobis hodie gratte, gramen; & (ut in priori) ṗtapa, nobis heppe gressus; in posteriori, hopp quod nobis mansit, saltatio, saltus, quasi per gramen gradiens, aut gramine saltans, saliénsve. Vulgo Grasshopper.
units.tr: Spinco, grasshopper. Derived (unless I am mistaken) from leaping, since the locust is accustomed to propel itself by a leap. To leap is among us "springing." The infant leaped in her womb, Luke 1, ver. 41; that is (as our older translations render the place), "The Babe springang in her belly." Hence the Saxon for locust, "zæpṗtapa" and "zæpṗhopp": "zæpṗ," which among us is today "grass," and (as in the former) "ṗtapa," which among us is "heppe," a step; in the latter, "hopp," which remains with us for leap or jump: as if stepping through the grass, or leaping in the grass, or leaping through it. Commonly "grasshopper."

units.la: Spel, Fabulatio: & spelle, parabola: vide Wisspell] Fabulatio Sax. etiam ṗpell, vel potius ýoelṗpell. q.vana colloquia. Nam simpliciter, & proprie, ṗpel, (ut Verstegano jam observatum) sermo mysticus, Oraculum, Parabola: quae quidem explanare, sive exponere, (saltem metaphorice) Saxon. ṗpellian, Belg. spellen: quà qui callet arte, Spellman merito dicendus. Cognomentum hoc Glossographo nostro, f. m. viro de his literis optime merito, non tam proprium quam conveniens, & debitum.
units.tr: Spel, fable; and spelle, parable: see "Wisspell." For fable the Saxon is also "ṗpell," or rather "ýoelṗpell," that is, vain talk. For simply and properly, "ṗpel" (as Verstegan has already observed) is mystical speech, an oracle, a parable; and to explain or expound it (at least metaphorically) is Saxon "ṗpellian," Dutch "spellen." Whoever is skilled in this art may rightly be called a Spellman. This surname suits our glossographer, a man who has deserved very well of these letters: it is not so much proper to him as fitting and due.

units.la: Snitume;
units.tr: Snitume;

units.la: <bl>Sníamo</bl>, Velociter, Confestim: & alibi <bl>stamo</bl>] Vide <bl>Stsotunoon.</bl>
units.tr: Sníamo, quickly, at once; and elsewhere "stamo." See "Stsotunoon."

units.la: <bl>Solre</bl>,solium : an <bl>solartam</bl>?] Quod nobis a sollar.
units.tr: Solre, a seat or throne; or solartam? Which among us comes from "sollar."

units.la: <bl>Sotwilcan</bl>, & <bl>sotwels</bl>, Quacunq;] Hoc Sax. ͬpa ḥpilc.
units.tr: Sotwilcan, and sotwels, whatsoever: Saxon "ͬpa ḥpilc."

units.la: <bl>Stotingon</bl>, Increpatione. Nos pro stimulatione] Stimulatio nobis <bl>stng.</bl> Quidam etiam nostratium dicunt <bl>ts</bl> <bl>stonnes</bl>, pro stimulat.
units.tr: Stotingon, rebuke. Among us it stands for stimulation; stimulation among us is "stng." Some of our people also say "stonnes" for to stimulate.

units.la: <bl>Staf-swert</bl>, Framea] Et gladius, & framea, Saxon. ꝩpeopo, quod nobis <bl>stwoɿD.</bl> Hoc autem Verstegano nostro <bl>stasstweard.</bl>
units.tr: Staf-swert, a broadsword: both a sword and a framea (spear). The Saxon is "ꝩpeopo," which among us is "sword." Verstegan, our countryman, has this as "stasstweard."

units.la: <bl>Stedinust</bl>, stabilitatem] Nobis eodem sensu, <bl>stedDinesse.</bl>
units.tr: Stedinust, stability: among us, in the same sense, "stedfastnesse."

units.la: <bl>Stros</bl>,strati : vide <bl>Stoje</bl>] Sternere Sax. stṗepian; stratum, stṗepeᴅ, & stṗæᴅ; unde iis stṗæᴛ, nobis <bl>street</bl>, pro via, platea.
units.tr: Stros, strewn: see "Stoje." To strew is Saxon "stṗepian"; stratum is "stṗepeᴅ" and "stṗæᴅ," whence "iis stṗæᴛ," which among us is "street," for a way or thoroughfare.

units.la: <bl>Saelga</bl>, Armentum : & <bl>saegon</bl>, armento.
units.tr: Saelga, a herd (armentum); and saegon, to the herd.

units.la: <bl>Soligon</bl>, salsuginem] Sal Saxon. ꝩealᴛ, nobis <bl>salf.</bl>
units.tr: Soligon, saltness. Salt is Saxon "ꝩealᴛ," among us "salt."

units.la: <bl>Saitho</bl>; Nimis] Hoc Sax. ꝩpẏḥe s
units.tr: Saitho; Too much. The Saxon form of this is ꝩpẏḥe.

units.la: <bl>Saeto</bl>, Dolorem] Vide suprà <bl>Se-rin.</bl>
units.tr: Saeto, Pain. See above under Serin.

units.la: <bl>Suffe</bl>, Pestilentia.
units.tr: Suffe, Pestilence.

units.la: Snenat, Suenot, Coagulatus: vide Bequallit.
units.tr: Snenat, Suenot, Coagulated: see Bequallit.

units.la: Sule, Columna ; & sult, columnas] Hoc Saxonicum rylle, quod nobis manfit: felle enim, & ground-felle, nobis cujusvis structurae basis, vel fundamentum; magis autem specifice, magna trabs aedificio supposita ; Sax. alias znounopealle, h.e. substructio. Hinc nostratium felle. Belg. fuple, alias fuele, pro Limine. Limen autem Saxon. peopjrcpolve, alias Spnexpolo, unde nostrum thze-sholt.
units.tr: Sule, Column; and sult, columns. This is the Saxon rylle, which has remained with us: among us "felle" and "ground-felle" mean the base or foundation of any structure, and more specifically a great beam laid under a building. In Saxon it is also called znounopealle, that is, substructure. Hence our "felle." The Belgians have fuple, or otherwise fuele, for a threshold. The Saxon for threshold is peopjrcpolve, otherwise Spnexpolo, whence our "threshold."

units.la: Smerenne, Adipe] Hoc Saxonibus rmepre, de quo plura in Kuofmer.
units.tr: Smerenne, Fat. In Saxon this is rmepre, of which more in Kuofmer.

units.la: Sneve, Nivis] Hoc Sax. rnap, unde nostrum snow, quod Belgis sneew: Teut. schnee.
units.tr: Sneve, Snow. In Saxon this is rnap, whence our "snow," which the Belgians call sneew; in Teutonic, schnee.

units.la: Verba.
units.tr: Words.

units.la: Scathan sal, Damnabit. Vide Bescathot] Damnum Sax. rceaz: damnum faciens, rceapiz: innocens, unrceapiz. Hinc Graffator, eis rceapa: Piratici, rae-rceapaj? Hoc Belg. schaed, nobis hodie scatb, & scade: Unde Canem rapacem, a scadole (id est, scatbfull) curre dicimus. Saxonum rceapana rcnæpe, Latine sonat, Spelunca latronum.
units.tr: Scathan sal, He will condemn. See Bescathot. Saxon damage is rceaz, one doing harm is rceapiz, innocent is unrceapiz. Hence "graffator" (a robber). In Belgic it is schaed; among us today, scath and scade. Hence we speak of a ravenous dog as running from a scadole (that is, a scathful one). In Latin, the Saxon rceapana rcnæpe means a robbers' cave.

units.la: Scedewon, {a}scetenoon sal, Obumbrabit] Vide suprà Ʃefceðistoit.
units.tr: Scedewon, He shall overshadow: see above, Ʃefceðistoit.

units.la: scalðon, Increpuerunt. Nos fcbelden, & compositè, Ʃefcstalðen] Huic convenit nostrum to fcolðe, illo sensu.
units.tr: scalðon, They rebuked. We have fcbelden, and in compound, Ʃefcstalðen. Our "to scold" corresponds to this sense.

units.la: scurgt, Averte : vide Ʃefcurgt] Asvertere Sax. acÿpnan, alias cÿpnan ; aversio cÿpnunz : atque hinc, à viarum scil. & platearum diverticulis, ut in compitis, pluribus apud nostrates locis hoc homen olim inditum, quod postea ih Cerring mutatum, tandem transiit (ut nunc dierum) in Charing ; quomodo quadrivium sive compitum, illud nuncupatur in suburbiis Londinensibus, ab occidente, propè Westmonasterium ; Charing-crosse, vulgò dictum ; Crosse addito, ob crucem ibidem, ut in compitis solitum, ôlim erectam. Bepcÿpian etiam, ut & arcÿpian, Sax. separare, item amputare, radere, resecare, &c. vulgò tó Theare, &c.
units.tr: scurgt, Turn aside: see Ʃefcurgt. The Saxon "to turn aside" is acÿpnan, otherwise cÿpnan; aversion is cÿpnunz. Hence, from the side-turnings of roads and streets, as at crossroads, this name was once given in several places among our people. It was later changed to Cerring, and at last passed (as it is now) into Charing. So the crossroads in the western suburbs of London, near Westminster, is called Charing-cross in common speech, with "cross" added because a cross was once erected there at the crossroads, as was customary. Bepcÿpian, like arcÿpian, is Saxon for to separate, also to cut off, shave, cut away and so on; commonly "to tear," etc.

units.la: scutta, Excussit.
units.tr: scutta, He shook out.

units.la: Ʃo-sto, Destrues.
units.tr: Ʃo-sto, You will destroy.

units.la: stibtan, Ædificabis] Ædificare, Sax. ꝗ-ṡ[?]ṗ[?]ꝗ; ʃ
units.tr: stibtan, You will build. To build in Saxon is ꝗ-ṡ[?]ṗ[?]ꝗ; ʃ

units.la: stincan, Odorabunt] Odorare Sax.
units.tr: stincan, They will smell. To smell in Saxon.

units.la: {a} ... ʒeꝛᵹτincʒan ? <bl>stinke</bl> autem nobis hodie vox est sensus ex diametro contrarii,cùm pro Fœtore sumatur.
units.tr: {a} ... ʒeꝛᵹτincʒan? Among us today "stinke" is a word of opposite meaning, since it is taken for a stench.

units.la: <bl>Stoꝁida</bl>, Irritavit: ut nos Metaphoricè <bl>stoken</bl>] Pungere Sax.ꝛᵺician, stimulus ꝛᵺiccelʃ ?
units.tr: Stoꝁida, He provoked: as we say metaphorically "stoken." To prick in Saxon is ꝛᵺician; a goad is ꝛᵺiccelʃ?

units.la: T
units.tr: T

units.la: <bl>Sefeꝁoon</bl>, Dexteram: & <bl>thefeuun</bl>, dextera : Vide <bl>Forthoza</bl>.
units.tr: Sefeꝁoon, right hand; and thefeuun, right hand: see Forthoza.

units.la: <bl>Thegenlιche</bl>,Viriliter. Nos <bl>degent-</bl> <bl>ljk</bl>, paullò alio sensu]<bl>Degben</bl>, <bl>Degben-man</bl>, (inquit Kilian.) Athleta, Pugil; vir præstans, strenuus, fortis.
units.tr: Thegenlιche, Manfully. Among us "degentlik," in a somewhat different sense. Degben, degben-man (says Kilian): an athlete, a fighter; a man outstanding, vigorous, brave.

units.la: Tales, Sax.nostrorum olim Deznei*, Latinè Thani, viri scil.honorati, ut qui gradu, virtute, fortunis, atque æstimatione, cæteris præluxerunt: præsertim si de classe eorũ essent qui regii dicti, vulgò cẏnınʒeꝛ ˢdeʒneɼ:alii enim inserioris erant classis, mediocres dicti, vulgò lerɼe ˢdeʒneꝛ ?
units.tr: Tales: among our forebears, Saxon Deznei, in Latin Thani, that is, men of rank who outshone others in position, valour, fortune and esteem, especially if they belonged to the class called royal, commonly "king's thanes." Others were of a lower class, called mediocre, commonly "mean thanes."

units.la: <bl>Thiat</bl>, Gens: & <bl>thiade</bl>, gente: & <bl>theado</bl>, gentium: & <bl>thiadon</bl>, nationes: & <bl>thiede</bl>, gentes] Sax.Gens, Populus, <bl>ˢeoɔ</bl>: gentes <bl>ˢeoɔa</bl> ?
units.tr: Thiat, people; thiade, of the people; theado, of peoples; thiadon, nations; thiede, peoples. In Saxon, people or nation is ˢeoɔ, peoples ˢeoɔa.

units.la: <bl>Thiadekunni</bl>, Generationes. Vide <bl>Kunt</bl>.nam compositum est]Vide etiam <bl>Thiat</bl>. <bl>Thin</bl>
units.tr: Thiadekunni, generations. See Kunt, for it is a compound. See also Thiat. Thin.

units.la: <bl>Sbhnnengqn</bl>, Tempora capitis] Hoc Sax. prifcis <bl>Ƨuhpenʒan</bl>; modernis autem, ut mihi author est Martinius, in Etymolog. <bl>Ꝺuennunge</bl>, & <bl>Ꝺuenne</bl>.
units.tr: Sbhnnengqn, temples of the head. In older Saxon this is Ƨuhpenʒan; in modern usage, as Martinius tells me in his Etymologicon, Ꝺuennunge and Ꝺuenne.

units.la: - <bl>Sbto</bl> Femur. Nos <bl>Ꝺtø</bl>] Sax. <bl>Ꞓeoþ</bl>; nos <bl>tbtgb</bl>.
units.tr: Sbto, thigh. Saxon Ꞓeoþ; ours tbtgb.

units.la: <bl>Sburtbtc</bl>, Egenus ! & <bl>thurtegtn</bl>, egeno] Scribendum forte <bl>thurfbtc</bl>, & <bl>thurtegtn</bl>. Teut. enim egenus, indigus, olim <bl>Ꝺoiftigb</bl>, <bl>Ꝺurftigb</bl>; hodie (littera r. transpofita) <bl>Ꝺioftigb</bl>, <bl>Ꝺuftigb</bl>, Sax. eodem sensu, <bl>Ꞓeanþ</bl>.
units.tr: Sburtbtc, needy; and thurtegtn, to the needy: perhaps it should be written thurfbtc and thurtegtn. For the Teutonic egenus (needy, in want) was formerly Doiftigb or Durftigb; today, with the letter r transposed, Dioftigb or Duftigb. The Saxon has the same sense: Ꞓeanþ.

units.la: <bl>Sbutoe</bl>, Ancillæ: & <bl>thutwon</bl>, & <bl>thiutwon</bl>, idem] Hoc Sax. <bl>Ꞓeopins</bl>, & <bl>Ꞓeopne</bl>.
units.tr: Sbutoe, maidservants; and thutwon, and thiutwon, the same. In Saxon these are Ꞓeopins and Ꞓeopne.

units.la: - <bl>Sothitf</bl>, & <bl>fotifbf</bl>, Apud.
units.tr: Sothitf, and fotifbf, Among, with.

units.la: . <bl>Sonferes</bl>, Venefici. Nos <bl>toonerers</bl>.
units.tr: Sonferes, sorcerers. Ours are toonerers.

units.la: <bl>Crego</bl>, Dolor: & <bl>tregon</bl>, dolore: & <bl>trege</bl>, dolores: & <bl>tregbaff</bl>, dolens] Tribulare, Saxon. <bl>τρέχιαh</bl>. Hinc (forte) parturientis fœminæ dolores, nobis <bl>tbiotwes</bl>: nisi malis à <bl>Ꞓpopian</bl>, quod Sax. pati sonat, unde Salvatoris nostri passio <bl>Ꞓpopunʒe</bl> dicta.
units.tr: Crego, pain; tregon, in pain; trege, pains; tregbaff, grieving. To suffer tribulation, Saxon τρέχιαh. Hence, perhaps, the pangs of a woman in labour, among us tbiotwes; unless you prefer to derive it from Ꞓpopian, which in Saxon means to suffer, whence our Saviour's passion is called Ꞓpopunʒe.

units.la: . <bl>Srilon</bl>, Fimbriis.
units.tr: Srilon, fringes.

units.la: <bl>Srifetwoʒtn</bl>, Thesaurus.
units.tr: Srifetwoʒtn, treasure.

units.la: <bl>Srtambon</bl>, Tubæ. Nos <bl>(trompen</bl>] Vide supra, <bl>Ꝺtambon</bl>.
units.tr: Srtambon, trumpets. Ours are "(trompen": see above, Ꝺtambon.

units.la: Iiʒ <bl>Sbtifeldaʒ</bl>
units.tr: Iiʒ Sbtifeldaʒ

units.la: Ꞓholon, Patientur: & tholinDon, patientibus: & tholoDtf, fuftinuiffem: tholoda, tribularer] Pati, Sax. Solian; paffus, Soloo: patientia, ȝeþylo: patiens, Sylo1ȝeno. Teut. Dulden.
units.tr: Ꞓholon, they will suffer; and tholinDon, to those suffering; and tholoDtf, I had endured; tholoda, I was afflicted. To suffer in Saxon is Solian; having suffered, Soloo; patience, ȝeþylo; patient, Sylo1ȝeno. In Teutonic, Dulden.

units.la: Ꞓhunfi, Extraxifti] A ȼeon forte, quod Sax. trahere; quibus extrahere, ꝑnam aȼeon ?
units.tr: Ꞓhunfi, you drew out. Perhaps a ȼeon, which in Saxon means to draw; with which "to draw out" (extrahere)... what is aȼeon?

units.la: Ꞓhurofremsoos, Perfecifti: & thurofremig, perfecta: & thurefremigero, perfecto: & thuroframinggon, confummati] Quod perfectū, nobis thozongbframeD: Sax. autem fulfpemeo: priore compofito à Saxon, Sups, nobis thzongb, & thozotw, i.e. per, & fpnemeo, nobis frameD, i.e. factum: posteriore vero à ful, nobis full, plenus, & eodem fpemeo, quod à fpemian fluit: unde nobis frame, pro fabricā; fo frame, fabricare.
units.tr: Ꞓhurofremsoos, you perfected; and thuroframig, perfected; thurefremigero, to the perfect; thuroframinggon, consummated. What is perfected, among us thozongbframeD. In Saxon, however, it is fulfpemeo. The former compound comes from the Saxon Sups, among us thzongb, and thozotw, that is, "through," and fpnemeo, among us frameD, that is, made. The latter comes from ful, among us full, full, and the same spemeo, which flows from spemian; whence among us "frame," for a fabric; so "frame," to fabricate.

units.la: Ꞓharolifton fal; Pertransfibit. Nos Doozlpden] Vide Farlithon; ubi de posteriori compositi parte: de priore vero in verbo hīc praecedente.
units.tr: Ꞓharolifton sal; It will pass through. Ours is Doozlpden: see Farlithon, where the latter part of the compound is treated; the former part is treated in the word preceding this one.

units.la: Ꞓtan, Enutries. Nos Ꞓpen & Dp: tpen] Vide suprà Ꞓhton fullun.
units.tr: Ꞓtan, they will nourish. Ours are Ꞓpen and Dp; tpen: see above, Ꞓhton fullun.

units.la: Ꞓtlo, Accelera: & tllont, festinant.
units.tr: Ꞓtlo, hasten; and tllont, they hasten.

units.la: Ꞓtlogon, Exercitationem: & Ꞓt-lon lon sal, Exercèbor : & Getlot, Exercitatus] Labor nobis Toile ; laborare, totolle : Saxon. etiam studia, quaestus, conatus, vylunzei adnitens, vylzeno.
units.tr: Ꞓtlogon, exercise; and Ꞓt-lon lon sal, I shall be exercised; and Getlot, exercised. Labour: ours is Toile; to labour, totolle. In Saxon also, studies, gains, efforts: vylunzei, striving; vylzeno.

units.la: V
units.tr: V

units.la: Wertbe, Itineribus : supra Gèvert-the] Ire, Iter facere, Sax. papan; de quo supra in Fàrlitboh.
units.tr: Wertbe, Itineribus: above, Gèvert-the] To go, to make a journey (Saxon papan), on which see above under Farlitboh.

units.la: Alta, Olla. Siburgi hodie, ulengasse, Platea Figulorum.
units.tr: Alta, Olla. Today at Siburgi, Ulengasse, Potters' Lane.

units.la: Unera, Reverentia : & unefoh, pudore] Revereri, Sax. unapian; ignominia unapé : ab an, Teut. hodie on, absque, & ane, honor, decus : quasi sine honore, decore.
units.tr: Unera, Reverence; and unefoh, shame] To revere (Saxon unapian); ignominy (unapé), from an, which in Teutonic is now on, meaning without, and ane, honour, credit: as if without honour or credit.

units.la: Underthudta, Subjecta : & Underthudiga, Subditi. Nos unoerdaeotcb] Subditi, Sax. unoepheo, ab eorum undep, (quod nobis manifit) subtus, & Seod, populus, gens.
units.tr: Underthudta, Subjected; and Underthudiga, subjects. We say unoerdaeotcb] Subjects (Saxon unoepheo), from their undep (which is plain to us), under, and Seod, people, nation.

units.la: Ungelceso, Vacuè] Vide Oferan-ungelcobt.
units.tr: Ungelceso, In vain] See Oferan-ungelcobt.

units.la: Unsuoti, Molesti] Quasi unsuoet, i.e. haud suaves.
units.tr: Unsuoti, Troublesome] As if unsuoet, that is, not pleasant.

units.la: Un, Usque : & untes, donec : & unt, idem] Nobis hodie unttl.
units.tr: Un, Until; and untes, until; and unt, the same] Today we have "until."

units.la: Unbewoltan, Immaculatus] For-san san rectius <bl>unbetwollan</bl>, quasi ab <bl>un</bl> privante, & <bl>betwollan</bl>, maculatus, inquinatus, à <bl>buple</bl> fluente, Sax. <bl>ful</bl>, nobis <bl>tolwle</bl>, turpis, immundus, q. d. (ut nostrates vulgo) <bl>unbefotwllen</bl>.
units.tr: Unbewoltan, Immaculate] Perhaps more correctly unbetwollan, as if from un, privative, and betwollan, stained, defiled, from buple, flowing (Saxon ful, ours tolwle, foul, unclean), that is (as our people commonly say) unbefouled.

units.la: <bl>Umbtwatb</bl>, quare? quasi <bl>omtwat</bl>?
units.tr: Umbtwatb, why? As if omtwat?

units.la: <bl>Wolton</bl>, Timore] Tremor, formido; Sax. <bl>fyphto</bl>. Unde noftr. <bl>frtgbt</bl>, & <bl>affrtgbt</bl>, illo sensu.
units.tr: Wolton, Fear] Trembling, dread (Saxon fyphto). Whence our frighten and affright, in that sense.

units.la: <bl>Urkundun</bl>, Testes: & <bl>urkunt-scap</bl>, testimonium. Est valde noscere: nobis manfit in formulis, <bl>Dtrkondt</bl>] Forte ab <bl>ober-cun</bl>.
units.tr: Urkundun, Witnesses; and urkunt-scap, testimony. It is well worth knowing. It remains with us in formulas. Dtrkondt] Perhaps from ober-cun.

units.la: <bl>Ursagon</bl>, Excusationes. Valde & multa dicere] q.d. <bl>ober-sap</bl>. Quatenus autem Excusationes notat, idem videtur ac <bl>Farsagon</bl>, de quo vide supra, <bl>Farseggent</bl>.
units.tr: Ursagon, Excuses. Speaking at length and much] That is, ober-sap. But insofar as it denotes excuses, it seems the same as Farsagon, on which see above under Farseggent.

units.la: <bl>Utriflon</bl>, Extremis. Nos <bl>vupterften</bl>] Hoc nobis <bl>uttermoft</bl>, Sax. ytemerta, unde noftrum <bl>ufmoft</bl>.
units.tr: Utriflon, Extremities. Ours vupterften] This is our "uttermost" (Saxon ytemerta), whence our "utmost."

units.la: <bl>Wala</bl>, Abyssus: <bl>wal</bl>, idem] Abyssus, profundum, Saxon. neopolnerpe ? <bl>Wala</bl> autem, ut & nostratium <bl>well</bl>, puteus, à Sax. paellen, & pellen, bullire, unde etiam <bl>utwalle</bl>, infrà.
units.tr: Wala, Abyss; wal, the same] Abyss, the deep (Saxon neopolnerpe?). But wala, like our "well," a spring, is from the Saxon paellen, or pellen, to boil up, whence also utwalle, below.

units.la: <bl>Walalteond</bl>, Beneplacito] Hoc nobis <bl>well-liking</bl>, à Sax. pellicunz; quod compositum à well, bene, & lcung, placitum.
units.tr: Walalteond, Beneplacito (goodwill): here we have "well-liking," from the Saxon pellicunz, which is compounded of well, well, and lician, to please (placitum).

units.la: <bl>Wambon</bl>, Utero] Venter, Saxon. pamb, unde nostrum <bl>wombe.</bl>
units.tr: Wambon, Womb] Belly (Saxon pamb), whence our "womb."

units.la: <bl>Wan</bl>, spes.
units.tr: Wan, hope.

units.la: Wanda, Vestimentum: & waf,vestem, vestimenta] Quod ad prius; Involucrum sive lineum cadaverale,(quia cadaver eo involvitur) nos dicimus a winding-sheet: Quod ad posterius; vestis & vestimentum Saxon. paœa, & ʒepeœe: unde vel hodie vestes sive habitus lugubres,nobis mourning weeds. Fœnum agri. Mat. 6. v. 30. Sax. /Ɵceneɼpeoꝺ. q.agri vestitus.
units.tr: Wanda, Garment; and waf, garment, garments] As to the first: a shroud or cadaver-cloth (because the corpse is wrapped in it) we call a winding-sheet. As to the second: garment and clothing are Saxon paœa and ʒepeœe, whence even today mourning garments, which we call mourning weeds. Hay of the field, Matt. 6. v. 30. In Saxon, the clothing of the field.

units.la: <bl>Washemo</bl>.Fructus: à crefcendo: & <bl>wasmo</bl>, idem] Fructus, Sax. paɼɣm; Fructifer, paɼɣm-bapenoe?
units.tr: Washemo, Fructus (fruit): from crescendo (to grow), and wasmo, the same. Fructus is Saxon wæstm; fruitful is wæstmbærende.

units.la: <bl>Welmo</bl>, Singulos.
units.tr: Welmo, Each one.

units.la: <bl>Werolt</bl>, Sæculum: & <bl>werold</bl>, & <bl>werild werilda</bl>: sæculum sæculi] Sax. peopulo e,unde nostrum <bl>wo;ld</bl>: quod Belg. <bl>wereld</bl>: Teut. <bl>werld</bl>.
units.tr: Werolt, Saeculum (age, world), and werold, and werild, werilda: saeculum saeculi (the age of ages). Saxon worold, whence our "world," which the Belgians have as "wereld" and the Teutons as "werld."

units.la: <bl>Wether</bl>,Nunquid?] Hoc nobis cum aspiratione, <bl>whether.</bl>
units.tr: Wether, Whether? With us, this, with an aspirate, is "whether."

units.la: <bl>Wige</bl>,Prælium, bellum: & <bl>wigis</bl>, belli: & <bl>wiga</bl>, prælia. Reperio & <bl>wie</bl>, bellum] Sax.pıʒa, heros: picɼtop,castrum, castellum: pizpur, specula; pizrteal, propugnaculum.
units.tr: Wige, Battle, war; and wigis, of battle; and wiga, battles. I find also wie, war] Saxon wiga, hero; wicstop, camp, castle; wizpur, watch-tower; wizrteal, bulwark.

units.la: ꝏ icte, Holera: & wortt herba. Inde ꝏ irtefpurgum, Herbipolis]Eâdem notione Saxon. pyprʒ: unde hortus eis pyprun?
units.tr: Wicte, Vegetables (holera); and wortt, herb. Thence Wirtefpurgum, Herbipolis [Würzburg]] With the same meaning, the Saxon wyrt, whence perhaps the Saxon garden, wyrtun?

units.la: ꝏ irfcapanꝺis, Epulantis.
units.tr: Wirfcapandis, Feasting.

units.la: ꝏ ithersacco, Adversarius, quasi wedersaeb, aut wiedersagger] Eodem sensu Sax. piprpraca, quod etiam contradictorem notat, à piperprace, contradictio.: voce compositâ à piper, contra, adversus, & recʒan, (nobis to sap) dicere, vulgò hodie gatnsap.
units.tr: Withersacco, Adversary, as if wedersaeb, or wiedersagger] In the same sense the Saxon wiperpraca, which also means a contradictor, from piperprace, contradiction. It is a compound of piper, against, and recʒan (ours to sap, to say), today with us "gainsay."

units.la: ꝏ ittt, Prudentia] Vide ꝏ ewitt.
units.tr: Witt, Prudence] See Wewitt.

units.la: ꝏ ittuf, Lex: & wittute, lege: & wittuteʒagbere. legislator. A promulgando, & longè latéque spargendo] Malim ego à witt, Sax. piт, & ʒepit, sapientia, prudentia; quia leges sunt prudentum confulta, vel decreta. Unde prudentum in eam rem consessus Sax. dictus piвenaʒemoт, quasi sapientum conventus, à piвena, & ʒemoт, ita significantibus ꝺꞩagbere autem hic, in wittut ꝺꞩagbere, à Teuton. ꝺꞩaegben, quod ferre sonat.
units.tr: Wittut, Law; and wittute, by law; and wittuteʒagbere, legislator. From promulgating and spreading far and wide] I would rather derive it from witt, Saxon wit, and ʒepit, wisdom, prudence, since laws are the counsels or decrees of the prudent. Whence the assembly of the prudent for this purpose is called in Saxon witenagemot, as if an assembly of the wise, from wiena and gemot, which thus signify (wise men and meeting). Here, in wittut ꝺꞩagbere, the word sagbere is from the Teutonic saegben, which means to bear.

units.la: ꝏ iolango, Usquequo?] Hoc Saxonibus þu lanʒe, nobis <bl>botw</bl> long.
units.tr: Wolango, How long? To the Saxons, þu lanʒe; to us, "how long."

units.la: <bl>Wolligis</bl>, Utinam] Nos <bl>would</bl>, additis his, <bl>to God</bl>, plerunque. Sax.etiam ɩc polo, pro volui.
units.tr: Wolligis, Would that. We say "would," adding "to God," often. The Saxons also say ic polo, for "I would."

units.la: <bl>Wop</bl>, Fletus: & <bl>wophis</bl>, Genitivo : <bl>wopinoi</bl>,lugens] Sax.etiam Fletus pop,Genitivo popeṙ.Lugens autem eis peopeno, unde nostratium <bl>to weepe</bl>, & <bl>weeping</bl>.
units.tr: Wop, Fletus (weeping), and wophis in the genitive, wopinoi, weeping (lugens). The Saxon also has wop, weeping, with genitive wopes. Lugens is Saxon wopende, whence our "to weep" and "weeping."

units.la: - <bl>Wartist</bl>, Gigas.
units.tr: Wartist, Giant.

units.la: - <bl>Wrreton</bl>, Iniquitatibus. Quasi <bl>on-</bl> <bl>recht</bl>] Cui nost.<bl>unrigbt</bl> assonat.
units.tr: Wrreton, Iniquities. As if on-recht. Our "unright" resembles it.

units.la: <bl>Wtferdt</bl>, Exitus] Expeditio, Saxon. utɼapɛ, quod ab ut fluit, h.e.ex, vel extra, & fapan, ire, proficisci, de quo plura in <bl>Farlitbon</bl> supra.
units.tr: Wtferdt, Exit] Expedition. Saxon utɼapɛ, which flows from ut, that is, out of or outside, and fapan, to go, to set out, on which more above under Farlitbon.

units.la: <bl>Watlanolico</bl>, Defolatoriis] Vocem puto compositam ab ut, nobis out, i. e. extra, foràs, & <bl>tanden</bl>, stare, quasi solitarius, & per se, veluti in eremo, stans.
units.tr: Watlanolico, Desolate places] I think it is compounded of ut, our "out," that is, outside, abroad, and tanden, to stand, as if solitary, standing by itself, as in a wilderness.

units.la: Verba.
units.tr: Verba.

units.la: <bl>Wardiligodos</bl>, Delesti] Vide <bl>Far-diligo</bl>.
units.tr: Wardiligodos, Thou didst blot out] See Far-diligo.

units.la: <bl>Woʒretwet</bl>,Compungimini,quasi <bl>be-</bl> <bl>routwet</bl>] Pœnitere, deplorare, Belgis <bl>Weronwen</bl>, Sax.neoppian, & <bl>beneop-rian</bl>?
units.tr: Woʒretwet, You are pricked, as if be-routwet: to repent, to lament. In Belgic, Weronwen. Saxon neoppian, and beneoprian?

units.la: <bl>Ap-</bl>
units.tr: Ap-

units.la: <bl>Upflagoda</bl>, Diftulit: & <bl>upflagodos</bl>, diftulifti] Ab eâdem (ni fallor) origine ac noftratium <bl>flacħ</bl>, & <bl>flow</bl>, id eft, tardus, lentus: Sax. <bl>flac</bl>, & <bl>flape</bl>. Differre etiam nobis, <bl>to flagget</bl>.
units.tr: Upflagoda, He deferred; and upflagodos, thou didst defer] From the same origin (I think) as our flacħ and flow, that is, slow, sluggish. Saxon flac and flape. To defer is also with us "to flag" or "to flagget."

units.la: <bl>Utwalle</bl>, Scateat: de fontibus] Vide supra, <bl>wala</bl>.
units.tr: Utwalle, To gush out: of springs. See above, wala.

units.la: <bl>Walsban fal</bl>. Dominabitur] Dominari, Saxon. <bl>pealoan</bl>: Hinc dominatio, ditio, authoritas, præcipuè Regum & Principum, eis anpealo & <bl>pylbinz</bl>. Hinc etiam Sceptrum gubernare, nobis vulgò, <bl>to wello the Scepter</bl>, alias <bl>to twap the Scepter</bl>.
units.tr: Walsban fal, He will rule] To rule: Saxon pealoan. Hence domination, dominion, authority, especially of kings and princes, in Saxon anpealo and pylbinz. Hence also to wield the sceptre, which we commonly say as "to wield the Sceptre," otherwise "to sway the Sceptre."

units.la: <bl>Wanbas</bl>, Exiftimafti] Exiftimare, opinari, arbitrari, Sax. penan: unde noftrum <bl>to tween</bl>, eopse fensu: ut cum dicimus, <bl>I tween</bl>, id eft, Ego exiftimo. Qui fui ipsius opinioni nimium fidit, nobis dicitur <bl>to overtween</bl>, dum rem vocamus <bl>ouer-tweenting</bl>. Saxon. <bl>ofepp-</bl> <bl>penny yree</bl>?
units.tr: Wanbas, Thou didst think] To think, suppose, judge: Saxon penan. Whence our "to ween," in the same sense, as when we say "I ween," that is, "I think." One who trusts too much in his own opinion is said with us "to overween," when we call the thing "overweening." Saxon ofepp-penny yree?

units.la: <bl>Welida</bl>, Elegit] A pillan forte, Sax. i, e. velle, unde voluntas eis, ut & nobis, <bl>wille</bl>; votum, pilla?
units.tr: Welida, He chose] Perhaps from the Saxon pillan, that is, to will; whence the Saxons have will (wille), as we do; vow, pilla?

units.la: <bl>Wtepon</bl>, Flevimus: & <bl>twopendf</bl>, lugentes: & <bl>twopan twir</bl> ploremus. Vide <bl>Wop</bl>, supra.
units.tr: Wtepon, We wept; and twopendf, mourning; and twopan twir, let us weep. See Wop, above.

units.la: <bl>Wtllo</bl>,
units.tr: Wtllo,

units.la: <bl>Wallo</bl>, Possedit: & <bl>wfelde</bl>, possedisti] Eidem origini (forte) referenda hæc,ac <bl>waldan sal</bl>, supra, quod vide.
units.tr: Wallo, He possessed; and wfelde, thou didst possess] Perhaps these are to be referred to the same origin as waldan sal, above, which see.

units.la: <bl>Wilfonodon</bl>, Tribulaverunt: & <bl>wlfinunf</bl>, tribulant: alibi <bl>wlfinunf</bl>, & <bl>wiffinunda</bl>, tribulantes] Vide <bl>Gewiffenon</bl>, supra.
units.tr: Wilfonodon, They troubled; and wlfinunf, they trouble. Elsewhere wlfinunf, and wiffinunda, troubling] See Gewiffenon, above.

units.la: <bl>Weigoden</bl>, Vexaverunt] Vox (ni fallor) conflata ex Belg. <bl>wee</bl>, Sax. <bl>pap</bl>, nobis <bl>woe</bl>, dolor, miseria, (de quo supra in <bl>Gewetgit</bl>) & <bl>geden</bl>, quod à <bl>doen</bl> fluens, facere sonat.
units.tr: Weigoden, They vexed] A word (I think) compounded of the Belgic wee, Saxon pap, our "woe," grief, misery (on which see above under Gewetgit), and geden, which flows from doen, meaning to do.

units.la: <bl>Wedan sal</bl>, Induam. supra <bl>Waf</bl>] Quod vide.
units.tr: Wedan sal, I will put on] See above, under Waf.

units.tr: and were in use among the old English or Saxons before the corruption

units.la: nem linguæ, quæ posterioribus seculis contigit, erant
units.tr: of the language that came about in later centuries.

units.la: in usu: Horum, (quæ quidem hic repræsentantur)

units.la: in usu sunt hodieque, leviter immutata, pleraque:
